eintraege.titel: Here’s When We Expect Omicron to Peak
eintraege.kontext: We're in early 2022, the Omicron variant importance is raising across the globe and the New york times decides to represent the Covid pandemic evolution of the last 2 years.
eintraege.gestaltung:
The New York Times literally broke the internet with this circular streamgraph. The dataviz community is divided, trying to understand if this unconventional figure is pure genius or trash, since it does not respect most of the comon rules.

Hint: when so many people talk about a chart, there is probably something good about it!

eintraege.kontext: The covid crisis is a world wide pandemic and India is certainly not spared. Some volunteer decided to create a dashboard to help Indian politics to take information driven decisions.
eintraege.gestaltung: The dashboard's overview: an interactive bubble map of India on a dark base map, where each circle marks a district sized by its case count. A search box lets you jump to any state or district. Slick dark-mode design with smooth transitions.

eintraege.kontext: The flow of people across borders has long shaped our world. Data from the past 50 years of international migration helped National Geographic understand why people make the choice to leave and where they go. Less than 10 percent of these migrants are forced to flee; most are seeking a better life and move only when they can afford to.
eintraege.gestaltung: The article describes the evolution of the immigration of many countries using smoothed area charts. The last figure looks pretty much like a ridgeline chart that is usually used to compare distributions, but smartly used here to compare evolutions.

eintraege.titel: Russia, Gas, and the Ukraine Conflict
eintraege.kontext: Europe relies on Russia’s natural gas to help heat millions of homes, generate electricity and power factories. With Russian troops massed along Ukraine’s border, Europe’s heavy dependence on Russia is limiting its diplomatic options and threatening to throw its energy supplies into turmoil. This map describes what proportion of the gas supply is distributed to each European country.
eintraege.gestaltung: This viz is a choropleth map with a sankey diagram on top. The choropleth shows how much each country relies on Russian gaz. The sankey diagram (arrows) shows where the Russian gas is distributed.

eintraege.kontext: Mario Kart on Nintendo 64 is probably one of the most famous game of all time (at least it is for me 😃). In this chart Cédric Scherer visualized the world records to understand what's the best character to play with.
eintraege.gestaltung: A lollipop chart grouped by character. It's interesting to notice that character names are not aligned vertically, but displayed next to each segment for better readability.

eintraege.titel: Appearance of the Five Most Popular X-Men Characters
eintraege.kontext: A chart that studies the appearances of the most popular characters in Chris Claremont’s X-Men comics
eintraege.gestaltung: A set of aligned streamcharts with helpful annotations. Nice attention to details with striking color palette, great fonts and clear legend.

eintraege.kontext: Visualization of the time it takes to crack the 500 most common passwords by online guessing.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular lollipop chart where each item is a password. Sorted by rank and colored by category. Annotation for the most extreme password, cool split by category at the bottom.

eintraege.titel: Infections caught in laboratories are surprisingly common
eintraege.kontext: In the middle of a worlwide pandemic, some people wonder if covid-19 escaped from a Chinese lab. The economist checked the probability of this by comparing with other diseases.
eintraege.gestaltung: A simple barplot with the Economist's well known style signature. Note bars are displayed horizontally, each being labeled using a very readable manner.

eintraege.kontext: A tidy tuesday challenge looking at how many males and females enrolled at historically black colleges and universities.
eintraege.gestaltung: A dumbbell plot made with ggplot2. On top of the nice layout and annotations, it also have additional grouped mean and standart deviation for each year.

eintraege.kontext: Covid is everywhere in the news and every newspaper is trying to summarize the situation in its country. Le Monde is one of the most famous newspapers in France and does a pretty good job in its daily updated dashboard.
eintraege.gestaltung: A grid of small multiples, one tiny area chart per French department, each labeled with its name and code. The consistent small format lets readers scan and compare epidemic curves across all regions at a glance.

eintraege.kontext: A visualization of scientific publication citation network. More than 60M citations coming from more than 7k journals were considered. Goal was to look for patterns on how journals tend to cite each other.
eintraege.gestaltung: An interactive hierarchical edge bundling where each node is a scientific journal. A journal is linked with another through an edge if it cites it in one of its publication. Clicking on a specific journal highlights its connections.

eintraege.kontext: A visualization of Spain, looking a both inequality (using the Gini Index) and average rent prices.
eintraege.gestaltung: A dichotomous choropleth map with nice annotation, good looking color palette and a 2D color mapping.

eintraege.kontext: The Time Magazine published a Dual-Y axis chart showing the evolution of both the army budget and the Number of troops between 1980 and 2012. Jorge Camoes decided to transform it with his own chart type.
eintraege.gestaltung: The result is a connected scatterplot. I personally prefer it since dual Y axis are notoriously broken, but it's hard to know if people truly understand it when they're not used to it.

eintraege.kontext: Probably the most famous viz about vaccines. It represents the number of measle infected people measured over 70-some years and across all 50 states. It shows a clear trend of decline after vaccines were introduced.
eintraege.gestaltung: A clean heatmap that shows the number of cases per 100,000 people. Available for other diseases with similar result.

eintraege.kontext: In the early euphoria following the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989, Germany moved quickly to erase the scars of its Cold War division. But East Germany’s legacy remains visible in statistics. Die Zeit offers a set of maps showing the remaining discrepancies between the West and the East.
eintraege.gestaltung: A massive load of hexbin maps, showing various variables like the average income, the proportion of people called Ronny or the avera farm size. Smooth transition between variables and clean design.

eintraege.autor: G. Lupi, S. Quadri, G. Rossi, D. Ciuffi, F. Fragapane, F. Majno
eintraege.kontext: This visualization explores the story of Nobel prizes through years.Visualized for each laureate are prize category, year the prize was awarded, and age of the recipient at the time, as well as principal academic affiliations and hometown.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each dot represents a Nobel laureate, and each recipient is positioned according to the year the prize was awarded (x axis) and his or her age at the time of the award (y axis).

eintraege.kontext: Shipmap.org is an interactive map of commercial shipping movements based on hundreds of millions of data points from throughout 2012. The project's aim is to highlight for a broad audience the extraordinary scale of modern commercial shipping, the routes these huge vessels take around the world, the geographic spread of different types of cargo boats, and the amount of carbon dioxide they produce.
eintraege.gestaltung: The unique base map shows ocean depth and major rivers, while the ships can be viewed as a high-resolution animation of movements over time (the 'ships' view) or as a plot showing all the positions at once (the 'routes' view), optionally colour-coded by ship type. A Talkie voiceover with music introduction sets the scene and provides an explanatory tour of the map.

eintraege.autor: M. Stefaner, Y. Vishnevsky, S. Rogers, A. Cairo et al.
eintraege.kontext: An interactive explorer based on the weekly Google Trends data for hundreds of dishes and ingredients, gathered over 15 years. It allows investigating the seasons and rhythm of food around the world
eintraege.gestaltung: The main viz of this project is a radial diagram. One viz per ingredient. The color of each square is for the year. The distance to center (radius) is for the number of google search.

eintraege.autor: A. Wattenberger, S. Greif and R. Benitte
eintraege.kontext: The State of Js is a survey that describes how Javascript (a programing language) evolved in the past few years. In the chart below they describe what libraries are trending, and which one are slowly disappearing. The whole webpage is awesome and you should definitely take a look.
eintraege.gestaltung: My favorite grouped connected scatterplot! Each line goes from 2016 to 2020. A higher point means a technology has been used by more people, and a point further to the right means more users want to learn it; or have used it and would use it again.

eintraege.titel: Quantifying the evolution of individual scientific impact
eintraege.kontext:
How does the impact of a scientist's work change over a scientific career? Does impact, arguably the most relevant performance measure, follow predictable patterns? Can we predict the timing of a scientist’s outstanding achievement? Kim checked the evolution of scientific author citation levels to answer those questions.

The result is called the random impact rule: the highest impact paper of a researcher can be anywhere in the sequence of papers!
eintraege.gestaltung: Each row is a scientist. From left to right, the first to the last paper of a scientist are arranged, ignoring their timing of publication. The line height shows the number of citation of the paper. The app has nice controls on top, including interactive histograms that I really like.

eintraege.titel: Rappers, Sorted by Size of Vocabulary — scatterplot
eintraege.kontext: A projects that compares the number of unique words used by some of the most famous artists in hip hop using each artist’s first 35,000 lyrics. Jedi Mind Tricks used 6424 unique words, compared to DMX that counts 2936.
eintraege.gestaltung: A one-dimensional scatterplot positioning each artist along an X axis of unique words used. Each artist is a small circular avatar, with vertical jittering to avoid overlap and an outlier labeled on the right.

eintraege.titel: Shifting Parent Work Hours, Mom vs. Dad
eintraege.kontext: Is it more common these days for dads to spend time with kids and work around the house? If so, is time spent that much different from decades past? How do dads’ times compare to moms’ times? An answer based on the American Time Use Survey that show hours spent with unpaid housework and childcare against hours spent at a job by moms and dads.
eintraege.gestaltung: 2 interactive histograms with animated transition between datasets and control buttons on top.

eintraege.kontext: On the 24th of February Russian troops invaded Ukraine. Le monde created a full page on the topic based on a map of the area.
eintraege.gestaltung: Not really dataviz since this map does not display any data. But still interesting for design inspiration, notably for the whole page layout.

eintraege.titel: At least half a million refugees flee Ukraine
eintraege.kontext: The New York Times covered the migration of Ukrainians fleeing the war with a very complete article full of migration maps.
eintraege.gestaltung: This snapshot shows a sankey diagram drawn on top of a map. Read the article for more map examples.

eintraege.kontext: Compared to the financial crisis in 2008, how much more or less do you have to pay for a Big Mac today?
eintraege.gestaltung: A clean line chart allowing to compare the evolution of several groups. Note the clean inline legend that avoids the spaghetti effect.

eintraege.kontext: A good proportion of the world countries have applied heavy sanctions to Russia following the Ukraine invasion. As a result the Rouble value is quickly decreasing.
eintraege.gestaltung: A line chart of the Ruble / USD exchange rate evolution. Two things are interesting here. Annotations are very clear and truly make a difference in the chart quality. The Y scale is inverted which is usually a bad thing, but works well here.

eintraege.kontext: In the 1970s, the most common household type in the U.S. was a married couple with kids. But over time, as people wait longer to get married and have fewer kids (if any), it’s grown more common to live alone or with non-family.
eintraege.gestaltung: This project describes this kind of effect using an alluvial diagram, showing both the rank and the percentage of each household type over the years.

eintraege.kontext: The share of Americans not having sex has reached a record high. The washington post made a full article on the topic, explaining why this is mainly due to young people which sounds scary to me.
eintraege.gestaltung: A simple timeseries line chart showing the evolution of 2 groups (male and female). Note the on-chart annotation of both the group names and the current values.

eintraege.kontext: Erasmus is an exchange program allowing students to study abroad for a semester or more. This figure allows to see which countries are the most involved.
eintraege.gestaltung: The chart is a mirror barplot, showing both the number of outgoing and incoming students. I love the general layout and visual, even though I'm not sure about the opacity used to encode the year.

eintraege.kontext: The war in Ukraine has made Russian social-media users glum. Posts on Twitter became far sadder than at the start of the covid-19 pandemic. A proof using sentiment analysis.
eintraege.gestaltung: A timeseries where evolution is represented using circles (average per day) and a line (7-day average). Having both information on the same figure is truly insightful. And the annotation of the outlier weeks help understand the full story.

eintraege.titel: Cat rescues by the London fire brigade
eintraege.kontext: How many cats are rescued by the London fire brigade each year? How does it compare with other animals? An answer with data, split by suburbs
eintraege.gestaltung: Each item of the small multiple is a suburb. For each, we quickly see the number of cats (blue line) and other animals (red lines). Coloring the area between both in blue or red makes it easy to compare both at a higher scale.

eintraege.kontext: A deep look into the 7102 known languages alive in the world. What are the main ones? In which country are they spoken?
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular Voronoi diagram showing the importance of each language. So much information packed on the same figure, in a very eye-catching style.

eintraege.titel: Hong Kong and the Omicron variant — stacked barplot
eintraege.kontext: Hong Kong’s vaccination rate has lagged far behind peer countries, especially among the most vulnerable. This article by the financial times goes deep into this matter and compares the situation with other countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: A set of three stacked bar charts comparing vaccination status by age group for Hong Kong, Singapore and New Zealand. Hong Kong's panel stands out with a large unvaccinated share among older age groups, while the peer panels are nearly fully vaccinated.

eintraege.kontext: A transect from the Swiss Alps over the Swiss lowlands to the Jura mountains.
eintraege.gestaltung: A very clean 3D map made with R with a minigraph, very clean and concise.

eintraege.kontext: Analyse the features of 3 penguins species: show the relationship between bill length and flipper length
eintraege.gestaltung: A custom scatterplot with auto-positioned labels to explore the palmerpenguins dataset made with R and the tidyverse.

eintraege.kontext: A scatterplot that shows the relationship between the Human Development Index and the Corruption Perceptions Index.
eintraege.gestaltung: A scatterplot with regression fit and automatic text repel. Relationship is striking.

eintraege.kontext: Compares the bill length, bill debt, flipper length and body mass of 2 penguin species.
eintraege.gestaltung: A radar chart that compares the features of 3 groups for 4 numeric variables.

eintraege.kontext: This Visualisation shows the cummulative length of tracks, the amount of tracks and the mean gain in elevation per location for a set of hikes in the Washington area.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular barplot with clear group annotation, nice layout and great on-chart legend to explain what's shown.

eintraege.kontext: A deep comparison of child labour across the globe.
eintraege.gestaltung: A line chart next to an area chart. Note that the first one is used for a percentage (does not make sense to add numbers up), when the second is used to a number where we are interested in the total number (stacking makes sense)

eintraege.kontext: Warming stripes reflect a minimalist style, conceived to use colour alone to avoid technical distractions and intuitively convey global warming trends to non-scientists.
eintraege.gestaltung: Warming stripes (sometimes referred to as climate stripes, climate timelines or stripe graphics are data visualization graphics that use a series of coloured stripes chronologically ordered to visually portray long-term temperature trends.

eintraege.kontext: A boxplot can hide the real underlying distribution of a set of data. The violin chart is a great alternative.
eintraege.gestaltung: Combination of a violin plot with a boxplot. Sample size added on the x axis. Build with ggplot2.

eintraege.kontext: The whole planet is trying to get vaccinated. Some people don't want to. Does an FDA approval would convince them?
eintraege.gestaltung: Using 3 waffle charts to compare 3 proportions.

eintraege.kontext: Random data are used here.
eintraege.gestaltung: This example just shows the default style of the Seaborn Python library.

eintraege.kontext: Covid19 Pandemic got a massive impact on some company revenues. This chart studies how revenues evolved during and after the pandemic.
eintraege.gestaltung: A Scatterplot that split the graph area in 4 sections, showing 4 potential behaviour of companies. As often, single data points are labeled to understand what are the most important data points.

eintraege.kontext: How many states are controled by which party in the US. How did it change between 2010 and 2020?
eintraege.gestaltung: Two parallel charts showing the evolution of each political party, measured by state and by district.

eintraege.kontext: A visualization of what parts of the piano keyboard are played the most in well-known classical music pieces.
eintraege.gestaltung: A bubble chart where the Y axis is a categoric variable. Very clean design, with an extensive legend.

eintraege.titel: The Art of the High Line
eintraege.kontext: The High Line is a elevated linear park in New York that showcases the work of artists. This viz describes the artists that have been exposed there.
eintraege.gestaltung: This piece is mainly a circular barplot. But it manages to store a massive amount of information thanks to the inner circles supplementary charts.

eintraege.kontext: This viz compares carbon tax features of several countries. It checks the revenue, the tax rate and the emmisioins portion covered by Tax.
eintraege.gestaltung: It's hard to classify this poster in a viz type. Each country is represented by several shapes, with shape size mapped to a numeric variable. Small multiples is used here to showcases all countries.

eintraege.kontext: 90% of malaria cases occur in Africa. That’s 200m infections and 400,000 deaths, mainly children under the age of 5. But the numbers are falling.
eintraege.gestaltung: A slope chart showing the # of cases per 1000 people in 2007 and 2017 for several African countries. A good way to highlight the global decrease while ranking the countries.

eintraege.kontext: Cycling is getting more and more popular on planet earth. This viz checks what are the cities with most bicycle commuters.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular packing chart with one level of information. Each bubble map is sized according to its proportion of bicycle commuters. I'm not a big fan of the gradient effect though.

eintraege.kontext: An animated map of global weather conditions. Includes wind, waves, temperature and much more. Show real time data.
eintraege.gestaltung: An interactive map showing global flows. You can rotate and zoom the globe. I like how the webpage is viz focused, with an optional control panel to decide what to display.

eintraege.kontext: A novel way to observe how wind blows on a geographical area. This work inspired Cameron Beccario to create the Global Weather Conditions app.
eintraege.gestaltung: Please read this article that explains how this project was born and what impact it had.

eintraege.kontext: A few vizzes giving running stats. I do not have more details on the project, this is just a snapshot
eintraege.gestaltung: I don't know much about this project, but wanted to show it for its slick design. Be careful, the radial barchart is definitely not a good viz type.

eintraege.kontext: A project by github that takes a repository and visualize its content. Each circle is a folder containing sub-folders, down until files.
eintraege.gestaltung: Two things I really love on this circular packing project: the way labels are set around each circles, and the scrolly-telling that works like a charm.

eintraege.kontext: Where does citizen of each US state come from? Where they born in this state? Or are they from abroad?
eintraege.gestaltung: A small multiple map that quickly conveys a pretty complicated information. No wonders it became viral on twitter!

eintraege.titel: Art, Women posing and upvotes — line chart
eintraege.kontext: Do women who pose with their art on Reddit get more upvotes? Erin gathered reddit data on the topic to proove that yes, posing with your art helps getting upvoted, especially if you're a woman.
eintraege.gestaltung: A line chart on a log-scaled x-axis showing the percent of posts that scored X upvotes or more, with three declining curves comparing female posers, male posers, and other arts/crafts posts. Key thresholds are directly labeled on each curve and annotations explain the gap between posers and non-posers.

eintraege.kontext: An interactive visualization of the Obama's budget proposal. A powerful way to see where the money should go based on Obama's opinion.
eintraege.gestaltung: An interactive circle packing chart with great tooltip. The transitions between viz types are very smooth and make it a delight to explore.

eintraege.kontext: French presidential elections are happening soon. Le Monde wrote a in-depth article showing some of the candidate features: who talks the most on media, who's the richest, who has the best chances to win according to polls?
eintraege.gestaltung: Clean horizontal barplot ranking presidential candidates by media speaking time, each bar colored by party and topped with a circular candidate portrait. Values are labeled directly at the end of each bar in hours and minutes.

eintraege.kontext: The central piece of a study on the spread of QAnon in the german-speaking world. It shows the amount of QAnon related messages exchanged on Telegram.
eintraege.gestaltung: A large streamchart tracing the volume of QAnon-related Telegram messages over time, with an orange flow at top and stacked brown bands below. Numerous annotations point to key moments such as the spike around the Storming of the Capitol.

eintraege.kontext: Using advanced NBA stats to rank player performance against pay.
eintraege.gestaltung: A colorfull scatterplot with gradient. Original design choices, especially when it comes to the axes.

eintraege.titel: Airports and world's megacities — flight connection map
eintraege.kontext: Biggest cities tend to have more departing flights per day. But some cities don't follow the trend. This data-based article tries to explain it.
eintraege.gestaltung: A world map drawing curved flight-connection lines departing from cities, contrasting Paris (927 daily flights) with Kinshasa (only 13) despite both being 13-million megacities. Annotations and curved arrows guide the eye to the key cities.

eintraege.kontext: An exploration of the dining habits and companions of Americans.
eintraege.gestaltung: A scatterplot of the percent of meals eaten alone against age, with two color-coded series (2003 and 2015) overlaid with smoothed trend curves and labeled directly at the line ends.

eintraege.kontext: If you were to ask random Americans what income class they fall into, there’s a good chance they’ll say “middle class”. But what does that mean?
eintraege.gestaltung: Three colorfull barplots allowing to compare features of 3 groups. The article uses scrollytelling.

eintraege.titel: What is Congress tweeting about? — barplot
eintraege.kontext: An article describing the topics that dominate members of Congress public discourse.
eintraege.gestaltung: A horizontal ranked bar chart on a dark background showing the share of tweets per topic (Health, Military, Education, etc.), with each bar labeled by its percentage and topic name in a matching color. Two thin stacked bars below compare this month versus last month.

eintraege.titel: Switching between phone brands — partial chord build-up
eintraege.kontext: A study asked 2000 residents of the Netherlands about their mobile phone behavior. The respondents gave information about the brand of their current main phone, and the brand of their previous main phone, and their answers are visualized in this data story.
eintraege.gestaltung: An early storytelling step of a chord diagram, where only a subset of ribbons is drawn so the reader can follow the flows out of a single brand before the full picture appears. The phone brands are arranged around the circle with a colored arc per brand.

eintraege.kontext: A visualization showing the rise and recent surge of the number of satellites that orbit Earth for the “Graphic Science” magazine.
eintraege.gestaltung: A vertical streamgraph with a lot of annotations telling the story. Note that each group of the stream are divided in substreams that follow a 'bump chart' logic.

eintraege.kontext: Visualizing the insane number of digital trackers that you gather when you browse the web for the new York times.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is not exactly a network chart but more a diagram representing the day of a regular internet user. The design is very clean and definitely worth a read.

eintraege.kontext: Frontex is the EU coast and border agency. It is in charge of organizing the flights that send deportees back home. This viz shows this sad flow on the globe.
eintraege.gestaltung: The static version already does a great job at showing the flow thanks to subtle color gradients and icons. But the video is definitely worth a look to, as it depict the acceleration of the process in another way.

eintraege.kontext: Some figures for a shareholder letter & annual report. Four extensive visuals about the income statement, costs, regional and FTE growth.
eintraege.gestaltung: A vertical sankey diagram of an income statement, flowing from revenue sources down through costs and net revenue to total comprehensive income. Flows start with a soft green-to-white gradient and key nodes are directly labelled with figures.

eintraege.kontext: Since 2003 UNESCO safeguards an ever growing list of our Intangible Cultural Heritage and these days there are almost 500 unique cultural elements inscribed on the list.
eintraege.gestaltung: A network chart showing those cultural heritage items and their connections. The interactive version is available here.

eintraege.kontext: Each year, US cities give thousands of homeless people one-way bus tickets out of town. An 18-month nationwide investigation by the Guardian reveals, for the first time, what really happens at journey’s end.
eintraege.gestaltung: A flow diagram showing bus ticket recipients fanning out from a single origin city, with red strands rising to higher-income destinations (12%) and blue strands descending to lower-income ones (88%), paired with a vertical density curve on the right.

eintraege.kontext: Visualizing the number of babies born across different time frames; from weeks down to the minute, to reveal the role of scheduling & intervention in births.
eintraege.gestaltung: Those density charts are highly customized. They are made circular to show the cyclic nature of the data. The distribution is also spread around the median line, instead of using 0 as a baseline.

eintraege.titel: Words in the Lord of the Rings
eintraege.kontext: In this visualization you can find out how many words a member of the lord of the rings has spoken at each different location throughout the trilogy.
eintraege.gestaltung: This chart is looking a lot like a chord diagram but has nodes in the center of the figures. Check the interactive version for a better exploration.

eintraege.kontext: In this visualization you can find out how many words a member of the lord of the rings has spoken at each different location throughout the trilogy.
eintraege.gestaltung: Just a clean parallel chart. Great way to legend the chart using an inline color in the chart explanation on top.

eintraege.kontext: Checking where FM radios are broadcasting from, split by type.
eintraege.gestaltung: Probably more data art than data viz but I very like the global style of this map.

eintraege.kontext: Some awesome viz are posted on Reddit every day, on a channel called DataIsBeautiful. This viz checks how popular each viz became for a month. Only a few per day make it to popularity!
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a very specific grouped line chart. There are many groups. The value can only increase and data is recorded for 36 hours only. It results in a very original shape. The annotation on top allow to learn what titles where the most popular.

eintraege.kontext: Driving around your city, you’re probably somewhat aware of Avenues and Boulevards and Streets and Roads and so on. This project aims at showing where each type takes place.
eintraege.gestaltung: Those map are just representing what kind of area each place is (street, place, river..). A bunch of cities are available as prints here.

eintraege.kontext: A project that maps the 34 million road intersections in Europe. Visit the project to see other great images about roundabouts and empty places.
eintraege.gestaltung: It's important to understand that the process results in a population density map. But the “city lights from space” + “starry sky” effect is definitely working here.

eintraege.kontext: The author read a bunch of book in 2021, and track the progress of each book along the year. This viz allows to see which book she was reading at each period of the year.
eintraege.gestaltung: In my opinion this is a very clever way to represent this dataset. It allows to have a very global vision of the year, and to see which book behaviour. Check how Sapiens became a struggle, I did not finish it either!

eintraege.kontext: How do you visualize a genome collection of more than 44.000 soil microbes? A project that takes gene sequences of different kinds of soil organisms, and tries to find species and specimens that are biologically active against crop pests.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular dendrogram with thousands of tips arranged around the perimeter, where branches fan out from the center. Selected clades are highlighted with distinct color gradients (green, orange, red, blue) while the rest of the tree stays in neutral grey.

eintraege.kontext: This figure is part of a paper called 'Force-Directed Edge Bundling for Graph Visualization'. It represents the US airlines connections and studies a variety of bundling algorithms.
eintraege.gestaltung: You can read the complete research paper here, that compares different values for the bundling. It shows very well how useful can be bundling.

eintraege.kontext: An example showing the co-authorship network of a researcher. Vincent Ranwez is author of several scientific publications and counts more than 100 co-authors. How are those co-authors interconnected?
eintraege.gestaltung: Vincent Ranwez has about 100 co-authors, all represented by a node on the following chart. If two people have already been on the same paper, they are linked by an arc.

eintraege.kontext: A sankey diagram showing the flow of metals in Australia. Import, Export, waste, all the in and out are included.
eintraege.gestaltung: Clean and un-cluttered design for this Sankey diagram.

eintraege.kontext: Everyday, people leave a country to join another, creating migration flows. This img is a reproduction of a figure from this scientific paper that studies those flows.
eintraege.gestaltung: An insightful chord diagram showing migration flows between continent. I really like how easy it is to understand the direction of the flow thanks to the arrow and the start vs end position shift of the connection.

eintraege.kontext: A in-depth analysis of the european regions. It tries to explain why Budapest, Warsaw, and Lithuania split themselves in two.
eintraege.gestaltung: A clean choropleth map of the EU where each country is filled along a pink-to-green diverging scale representing economic development, from less developed to more developed. A horizontal gradient legend sits at the top.

eintraege.kontext: Not sure about the context of this chart, it's all written in flamish 😀 .
eintraege.gestaltung: Clean treemap with illustrations. The transition between dataset is nice in the first tries, but then feels a bit long when you keep playing with it.

eintraege.kontext: What if Google searches were used to award points in the Eurovision Song Contest? What countries would make the final and who would cry victory?
eintraege.gestaltung: Many countries are small, sometimes barely visible on the map. But they're value is worth as much as big countries. This article suggests to squarify Europe to put all countries on the same scale.

eintraege.kontext: The merging of AB InBev and SABMiller creates a brewing giant, more than one third of all beer worldwide will be produced by just one company. Here is an overview of all the beers that are concerned.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a radial dendrogram, where beers are subdivided in continent and country. Fun interactive touch: hovering a beer makes you see the bottle. Made me thirsty 🌴 !

eintraege.titel: Who speaks when in Shakespeare's MacBeth?
eintraege.kontext: Distribution of speech share (number of words) per character in each scene. Acts are separated with vertical lines.
eintraege.gestaltung: A dark mode streamgraph with clean annotations.

eintraege.titel: Mortality and mental disorders — line charts
eintraege.kontext: An interactive webpage that goes along with a scientific publication. The goal was to study the links between mortality rates and mental disorders.
eintraege.gestaltung: A small-multiples grid of line charts plotting mortality rate against age on a logarithmic y-axis, comparing people with versus without mental disorders (solid vs dashed lines). The right column shows mortality rate ratios with shaded confidence bands.

eintraege.titel: The World Mental Health Survey — heatmap
eintraege.kontext: A set of data visualization on comorbidity between mental disorders. This is a webpage that goes along this scientific publication, allowing readers to explore the data themselves.
eintraege.gestaltung: A large symmetric correlation matrix where each cell is colored on a viridis-to-magma gradient to encode the strength of comorbidity between pairs of mental disorders. Row and column labels are color-coded by disorder family.

eintraege.titel: End of the Covid-19 pandemic — scatter plot
eintraege.kontext: Mc Kinsey regularly post updates on the covid situation, especially concerning future potential trends. Luckily this report is full of nice visuals.
eintraege.gestaltung: A scatter plot on a logarithmic fatality-rate axis comparing infectiousness and lethality of diseases, with named circles for individual diseases and colored rounded rectangles showing estimated ranges for SARS-CoV-2 variants (Omicron, Delta, Alpha, ancestral strain).

eintraege.kontext: A migration map showing how french people are moving inside their country. What's really interesting here is that you can select a subset of the population based on sex or work category. Stunning result!
eintraege.gestaltung:
This migration map is very much inspired from the wind map of Tobler et al. that is also feature in dataviz-inspiration.com.
Note: the static visual is disappointing but the animated version is mesmerizing!

eintraege.kontext: Reported crimes that the police classified as hate crimes and where killer identified hate as the underlying motive.
eintraege.gestaltung: A simple yet clean horizontal barplot.

eintraege.kontext: St Vincent and the Grenadines is a southern Caribbean island country. The country is made of 32 islands, only 9 of them are actually inhabited. It is a tropical paradise visited by many people.
eintraege.gestaltung: The project is a mix between a map of the country and a sankey diagram.

eintraege.kontext: This visualization uses Google Trends to explore shopping interest for various products before and during the Covid-19 pandemic.
eintraege.gestaltung: A title slide built around a single large light-blue line chart tracking Google Trends search interest for 'cat treats' over time. A dated annotation marker flags the WHO's March 2020 pandemic declaration, with faint background lines hinting at other categories.

eintraege.kontext: Orion is a Figma plugin to quickly embed chart templates into a design system.
eintraege.gestaltung: A radar chart comparing two series across six financial categories, drawn as pink and blue polygons over a soft, layered concentric backdrop. Each axis is directly labeled with its category name and dollar value, giving it a clean futuristic look.

eintraege.titel: League of legend analytics — radar chart
eintraege.kontext: An analytics dashboard design to show your stats and help you improve at League of Legends.
eintraege.gestaltung: A radar chart comparing two players across eight gameplay axes (fighting, farming, vision, aggression, etc.), with glowing cyan and purple polygons over a faint concentric spider grid on a dark background. Each axis is marked with a small game icon.

eintraege.kontext: Dynamic Planning is a proof of concept for a SaaS planning platform that allows for data-driven decisions based on live building occupancy. In its current state, it is a data visualization dashboard that connects sensor data and institutional datasets to a building information model (BIM) in order to track an organization's planning goals.
eintraege.gestaltung: A stacked bar chart titled 'Stacked Bar Chart' showing people counts across building locations, with each bar segmented into colored categories using a warm-to-cool palette and rounded bar tops.

eintraege.kontext: There are 50 billions birds on this planet. The epsiloon mag (science popularization magazine) made a full page about bird classificatio, giving a pretty insightful result.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular packing chart showing the main chart families and their importance in term of number of animals. Annotation are in french but I love stories that are told around a chart like this.

eintraege.kontext: An infographic studying the biomass of marine organisms. It basically split organisms by size buckets, and check their total weights. Surprisingly, it's always clost to 1 gigatonne!
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular barplot showing the total biomass of each organism size bucket. Interesting to see that a lot of information has been added to it: circles to show the recent evolution of the values, stacking to split the value by organism type.

eintraege.kontext: Each city has its own microbiota. Researchers took samples in some major city metro stations. The viz checks which micro-organism is present in which city.
eintraege.gestaltung: Six treemaps allowing to understand and compare the behavior of 6 cities. The viz allows to understand how diverse the microbiota is in each city, but it's still hard to compare one specific specie across cities.

eintraege.kontext: When a mammal dies, it is about 5% of the time because of cancer. This inforgraphic checks which kind of mammal is more prone to get cancer and shows how spread this disease is.
eintraege.gestaltung: This viz is a dendrogram showing the classification of mammals. The distance to center of each node provides its life expectancy, and the node features (size and color) gives more info on the specie. All of that makes the figure very insightful imo.

eintraege.kontext: How different Houses of Game Of Thrones killed?. A project part of the 30 days 30 charts challenge
eintraege.gestaltung: A sankey diagram with just 1 origin and 1 destination. I like how it highlights that most murders happened from a dragon.

eintraege.kontext: We are in 2022 and the U.S. has reached 1 million deaths even as COVID has faded from the headlines. At this grim milestone, this project sought to refocus on the scale of loss suffered.
eintraege.gestaltung: Authors used growing rectangles to make us understand more the scale of numbers. There is a traditional line chart at the bottom right, but the big rectangles make the data more 'alive'.

eintraege.kontext: The design depicts global carbon emissions by country, colour-coded by continent and proportional to the amount of emissions. The arrangement of the spheres beautifully pays off the carbon footprint metaphor with a critical sense of scale.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a circular packing chart with very specific shape for the root node. It makes the visualization shine, and made it a dataviz well-known masterpiece.

eintraege.titel: Madagascar Relief Map — pink relief map
eintraege.kontext: Part of a project called '#rayshader adventures, an #rstats tale'. Many countries have their equivalent in the project. It is made with rayshader, an open source package for producing 2D and 3D data visualizations in R
eintraege.gestaltung: A 3D shaded relief map of Madagascar rendered with an eye-catching pink-to-magenta gradient that encodes elevation. The island floats on a clean white background with minimalist title typography.

eintraege.kontext: A visual representation on how Alli spent here time through her life, split by categories like caretaking, leisure, work and more. Inspired by Carni Klirs work.
eintraege.gestaltung: A great streamgraph, totally adapted at showing the evolution of each category through time in a flowing style. I really like the texture employed here, giving it a personal nature.

eintraege.titel: Spare time over a life time
eintraege.kontext: A visual representation on how Carni spent his time through his life, split by categories like time  wasters, career and more.
eintraege.gestaltung: Pretty insightful streamgraph. The first one afaik showing the evolution of one's life activities.

eintraege.kontext: The World Resource Institute (WRI) studies how to create a sustainable food future. It published a final report giving solutions to ensure the world can feed 10 billion people by 2050 in a sustainable way. It contains many great vizs.
eintraege.gestaltung: A waterfall (bridge) chart showing how a series of agricultural mitigation measures step down GHG emissions from a 2050 baseline of 15 Gt to the target. Each step is annotated with the specific intervention and grouped into shaded vertical bands by category.

eintraege.kontext: Untitled UI is the largest UI kit and design system for Figma in the world. Some of its components are dataviz related.
eintraege.gestaltung: A monthly stacked bar chart with three series rendered in a clean purple palette on a white background. Rounded bar tops and a simple dotted-marker legend give it a modern, polished look.

eintraege.kontext: Datylon is a data visualization platform dedicated to graphic designers and report designers who work with Adobe Illustrator. It is a robust chart maker plugin for Illustrator to create beautiful charts and graphs for inspiring data stories.
eintraege.gestaltung: A scatterplot showing NBA 2021-22 players' scoring efficiency, with the plane divided into four quadrants (effective/low-effective high/low scorers) and a zoomed inset of the top performers in the upper right.

eintraege.kontext: Greenhouse gas emissions are a hot topics nowadays. Le Monde wrote an article describing what part of our lifestyle have the strongest impact.
eintraege.gestaltung: A perfect treemap with impactful color sheme and a great design making it crystal clear what to do to decrease your personal effect on global warming.

eintraege.kontext: Receiving 'Nul Points' at Eurovision (failing to earn a single point) is the most dreaded outcome for any participating country. This viz visualizes the 37 times it happened, split by countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: A timeseries heatmap where each cell is represented as a dot. The cell can be empty (no participation), grey (earned some points) or orange when no points were earned.

eintraege.kontext: Not really dataviz related but I liked those colors and would love to re-use them on a bubble chart or related.
eintraege.gestaltung: Playing with color dodge / Color Burn / Overlay to create some good looking logos.

eintraege.kontext: A scrollytelling article (in french) that talks about health in Bruxelles, the capital of Belgium. It highlights the discrepencies that exist between suburbs. A in-depth investigation definitely worth a read.
eintraege.gestaltung: A dark, detailed choropleth map of Brussels shading individual building footprints along a teal-to-orange diverging scale, revealing a sharp spatial divide between neighborhoods.

eintraege.kontext: In 2014 there were about 10M elements in wikipedia. This infografic groups them by type (e.g. geographical entity) and checks what are the most numerous items.
eintraege.gestaltung: Beautiful infographic making the best of dark mode. I really like the slight gradients that truly make a difference on the final appearance.

eintraege.kontext: This is a correlogram made using the pairplot function of the seaborn python library for data visualization.
eintraege.gestaltung: Clean and simple correlogram. Distributions on the diagonal. Scatterplots on other facets.

eintraege.kontext: An overview of what R can provide when it comes to build correlograms.
eintraege.gestaltung: A ggpairs() scatterplot matrix showing five variables: lower triangle holds black scatterplots, the diagonal shows density curves, and the upper triangle prints pairwise correlation coefficients.

eintraege.kontext: Lisa tracked her plastic waste details for a year and wrote a blogpost full of insightful dataviz to explain the result.
eintraege.gestaltung: A dark, radial circular barplot radiating red bars from a central clock-like dial to show plastic use over time, paired with a bold annotated callout of 16kg of single-use plastic. Strong visual identity with a small bubble legend at top right.

eintraege.kontext: A deep dive into Reddit's most comon dirty words, trying to understand how those words are combined together.
eintraege.gestaltung: This heatmap does not have anything crazy in term of viz, but with more than 5000 likes on twitter it's one of the most viral viz I know.

eintraege.kontext: Analysis of all lip sync songs featured on different seasons of Drag Race across all franchises.
eintraege.gestaltung: Simple barplot with slick design and especially nice annotations.

eintraege.kontext: Windguru.cz is the most famous service for wind prediction, used by a myriad of surfers. It has a page for each spot, showing the most recent wind force and direction.
eintraege.gestaltung: The area chart is very powerful and informative. It displays both wind speed and direction, including gust values and average values. Color gradient allows to know what's happening in a glimpse.

eintraege.kontext: I've always been interested by viz that looks futuristic. This generative shape is good inspiration for this.
eintraege.gestaltung: Not a dataviz. But I would like to create a network chart based on this design.

eintraege.kontext: A circular calendar showing the evolution of the most significant tech companies of our time. Show features like market value, purchase price, number of employees and more.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a circular lollipop chart. It displays a big amount of information for each company and I like the color choices that makes it look futuristic.

eintraege.titel: What it takes to go to space
eintraege.kontext: This visualization helps one understand the likelihood and probable career path one can take to become a NASA Astronaut.
eintraege.gestaltung: Vertical sankey diagram with stunning colors. I wonder how insightful it is with such a complexity in the data, but design is good.

eintraege.kontext: Not a real viz. This is a fiction user interface made for movies or video game. But some concept can definitely be borrowed to create real futuristic style dataviz.
eintraege.gestaltung: Many different chart types are represented, especially if you watch the whole video.

eintraege.kontext: A circular graph mimicking the shape of a tree. It represents immigration in the U.S: each dot represents 100 immigrants. Distance to the center represents the date. Angle represents the migrant origin.
eintraege.gestaltung: This chart is unique, it does not belong to any chart type I know. And that's probably what makes it so famous and inspiring. Awesome metaphor, probably closer to data art than dataviz though.

eintraege.kontext: This chart is a remix of Hans Rosling's famous gapminder bubble chart. It shows the evolution of life expectancy and fertility rate for a few countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a very unique connected scatterplot. Bubble size is mapped to the year, which ease the understanding of the evolution and making the flow very smooth. It truly allows to 'feel' the evolution of each country!.

eintraege.titel: Waves of Interest — density heatmap map
eintraege.kontext: Which topics capture the attention of Americans during US election years? And how have our interests shifted from one election cycle to the next? This project investigates these questions with the help of Google Search Trends data.
eintraege.gestaltung: A density 2D heatmap shaped like the contiguous United States, glowing with a blue-to-yellow gradient on a deep purple background to show the surge in Google search interest for 'Minimum Wage'. State labels carry direct percentage annotations like +105% and +68% over their hotspots.

eintraege.kontext: Since her debut in the 1990s, Serena Williams has spent a total of 319 weeks atop the WTA rankings, a tally that spans three time periods in her career.
eintraege.gestaltung: This chart is a vertical line chart. Making it vertical allows to fit many more annotation, what makes the chart very insightful.

eintraege.titel: Leonardo DiCaprio Refuses to Date a Woman Over 25
eintraege.kontext: A highly viral viz showing how Leonardo DiCaprio always broke with his girlfriend once she turned 25, even at 42 y.o.
eintraege.gestaltung: Not sure what made this viz viral. The topic? The eye catching look? The fact that it was originally made using excel? ggplot2 version.

eintraege.kontext: The result of a research paper on 51 countries and 1.3 M people. Trying to understand when people are the most happy, and why there is a mid-life dip.
eintraege.gestaltung: A line chart showing the relationship between happiness and age across several surveys. The chart could be greatly improved but I find the topic very interesting.

eintraege.kontext: Talks about gaz reserves in Europe. But I do not understand much about the article to be honest :).
eintraege.gestaltung: Marimekko chart.

eintraege.kontext: More and more countries achieve to decouple economic growth from CO₂ emissions.This chart shows the evidence for 25 countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: What strikes me here is that I'm not sure what kind of viz it is 🤔. But with 12k likes on twitter, the message is definitely conveyed efficiently.

eintraege.kontext: Distribution of salaries in France in 2020.
eintraege.gestaltung: I do not particularly like the look of the chart, but I like the annotation showing the sum value of a group of bars. 19k likes on twitter!

eintraege.kontext: A sad project tracking people who have died in the process of migration towards an internation destination.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular packing chart where each bubble is an incident that caused arms to migrants. Color related to origin location. Beautiful but sad.

eintraege.kontext: Not every country is truly facing an equal risk from climate change, nor has the capability to prepare and protect itself. This project highlights that countries with low readiness are often the most vulnerable, and the least responsible.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a scatterplot using squares instead of circles. It has a third dimension mapped to the square size. A toolip allows to get the name of each country with its precise numbers. Clean annotation. Nice hover effect. I love data wrapper.

eintraege.titel: How Britain ended its coal addiction — stacked area chart
eintraege.kontext: The shift in the UK is an important victory for environmentalists in their fight against fossil fuels.
eintraege.gestaltung: A stacked area chart of UK electricity supplied (TWhs) from 1980 to 2018, showing coal collapsing while renewables, nuclear and combined cycle gas turbine fill the void. Labels sit directly inside each colored band.

eintraege.kontext: A graph showing the striking difference between linguistic regions in switzerland concerning a recent reform proposal.
eintraege.gestaltung: Interactive beeswarm chart where each dot is a council. Split in 3 groups (one per region). Very cool to see an uncommon chart printed in a newpaper.

eintraege.kontext: A map showing the dominant tree species in Germany.
eintraege.gestaltung: A stunning map built with R and rayshader. Simply beautiful and insightful.

eintraege.kontext: A visual showing the number of flood phenomena in each of the European countries. A barchart on the left shows the most impacted countries. A stream chart on the right shows the evolution of the number of events.
eintraege.gestaltung: Data talks about floods, and the visual definitely goes along with it. The color palette and the organic shapes of the streamchart are going so well together. As often with nice visuals, the annotation tells the story.

eintraege.kontext: Some languages are about disappear from the planet. This visual quantifies this and shows where in the world those languages are.
eintraege.gestaltung: A clean world map with dots and 2d density on top. There is also a stacked barchart at the bottom showing how vulnerable the languages of each zone are.

eintraege.kontext: Carbon emissions is such a hot topic nowadays. This chart summarizes how much C02 a country emitts, in regard of its population
eintraege.gestaltung: This chart is a circular barchart with unequal bar widths. Indeed, bar widths are proportional to the country population. This is such an interesting tweak that makes the chart much more insightful.

eintraege.kontext: This view shows the number of hate crimes recorded by the police in UK. In particular, on the progress of thes crimes and against which category they are mainly carried out.
eintraege.gestaltung:
A time series showing the general trend on the left. On the right, a waffle chart with small multiple: instead of having all the groups on the same waffle, each group is represented on its own waffle.
It's a surprising strategy, but it works well to show the weight of each group on the whole.

eintraege.kontext: The graphic shows the correlation between Brazilian GDP (horizontal axis) and inequality (vertical axis). Each dot represents a year.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a connected scatterplot. It is very powerful as it shows both a correlation and an evolution on the same figure. However, it takes a while to understand it properly, so make sure to share it with an audience used to complex charts.

eintraege.titel: The slow loss — endangered birds dendrogram
eintraege.kontext: This diptych shows the species of endangered birds and fishes in Italy, according to the IUCN's 'Red list'. For each animal, the following are indicated: common name, order, degree of danger, size and habitat.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular dendrogram on a light background mapping endangered Italian birds, with warm-toned feather-like shapes radiating outward whose size encodes the animal. Small multiples of leaf/feather shapes run along the bottom as a legend.

eintraege.kontext: Elizabeth II, was the queen of the UK until the 8th of September. Liz Truss was prime minister from the 6th of September.
eintraege.gestaltung: A dataviz joke with a simple timeseries that gathered more than 100k likes.

eintraege.kontext: Top authors by decade. Ranking based on number of weeks author appeared on list. Sparkline depicts total weeks by year. Top performing book included beneath each author's name. Data from Post45 Data Collective.
eintraege.gestaltung: Such a clean table providing heaps of info. What I love the most is that it's been created using R.

eintraege.kontext: What is the relation between climate change and violent conflicts? Which role do socio-economic scope conditions play in exacerbating climate impact? How can we allow analysts and policymaker to make better decisions — based on heterogenous, multi-faceted information sources?
eintraege.gestaltung: A dark-themed world map rendered as a dotted choropleth, with hand-drawn outlined regions highlighting hotspot areas where climate impact, scope conditions and conflict overlap. A legend at the bottom maps colors to those three dimensions.

eintraege.kontext: An homage to the Beatles. It represents their core thirteen albums and breaks down every song in each album.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular layout displaying several layouts of information. Bubbles to show the total number of the word 'love' being said, line showing when it happened in the song.

eintraege.kontext: An infographic that looks at music genre popularity over time, based on billboard hot 100 frequency.
eintraege.gestaltung: A stream graph. What's interesting here is that it does not go straight from left to right, but does its own way. Definitely not a scientific strategy but increases the flow feeling of the data.

eintraege.kontext: How much of the gaz of European countries comes from russia?
eintraege.gestaltung: Smart way to represent info. Size of the square shows percentage of dependency to Russia. Then inner rects show usage of coal, gaz and petrol.

eintraege.kontext: An interactive map that shows you how far you can travel from a specific point in a specific amount of time.
eintraege.gestaltung: This kind of map is called isochrone maps.

eintraege.kontext: Since the presidency of Franklin D. Roosevelt, the Gallup polling organization has asked Americans an open-ended question: “What do you think is the most important problem facing this country today?”
eintraege.gestaltung: A set of treemaps made for the New York Times

eintraege.kontext: Checking who voted for what in Britain's election.
eintraege.gestaltung: An annotated geographic choropleth map of the UK colored by winning party per constituency, paired with a results table of seats and seat changes, with callout annotations explaining regional outcomes.

eintraege.kontext: Trump Vows to Stop Immigration From Nations ‘Compromised’ by Terrorism. How Could It Work?
eintraege.gestaltung: Some cartograms where each country is represented as a rectangle, with size proportional to the number of immigrants.

eintraege.kontext: Pandemic stimulus has made the world’s wealthiest wealthier. Ruchir Sharma charts the rise of ‘good’ and ‘bad’ billionaires around the world
eintraege.gestaltung: A horizontal stacked bar chart ranking countries by billionaires' wealth as a percentage of GDP, with a light segment for the 2020 share and a dark segment for the 2021 increase. Russia and Sweden top the list.

eintraege.kontext: Musk is now owning twitter. Shift in follower counts for Elizabeth Warren, Ted Cruz and others shows how the platform is beginning to change.
eintraege.gestaltung: It's very unusual to see a line chart displayed from top to bottom instead of from left to right. But since the figure is wider then tall, it increases the insight of the figure message. Smart move!

eintraege.kontext: A humorous Twitter account that tackles here the subject of excitement for work throughout someone's career.
eintraege.gestaltung: Not much to say about this chart, except that topic definitely makes a diff for virality 😋

eintraege.kontext: A Twitter account that describes itself as « the home of terribles maps with a pinch of humour », and that illustrates here the differences in numbers of pornstars in different European countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: This choropleth map is far from perfect, but the topic makes it highly viral.

eintraege.kontext: French graphic designer Clara Dealberto layed out the smallest town names by department in her country.
eintraege.gestaltung: Just a map with interesting labeling

eintraege.kontext: A Google keyword search comparison of ChatGPT and Lensa over a two week period in November 2022.
eintraege.gestaltung: Interesting way of labeling the 2 lines here. Inline labeling on the right hand side is usually used to avoid having a legend. But the labeling over the line allows to not waste real eastate!

eintraege.kontext: This visual depicts the share of men vs the share of women who smoke tobacco in different countries, in a more general inquiry about world smokers.
eintraege.gestaltung: This graph is a mirrored vertical barplot: left hand side is for women, right hand side for men. What's interesting here is that the bar height encodes a second numeric variable: the population size.

eintraege.kontext: This chart compares the number of paid vacation days in different countries around the world.
eintraege.gestaltung: A surprising way of showing a distribution: a scatterplot with jittering is used instead of a more classic histogram or density chart.

eintraege.kontext: 25 maps that illustrate the population densities of different countries in a very visual way.
eintraege.gestaltung: Using the very awesome RayShader to build stunning 3d maps with R.

eintraege.kontext: Thanks to all sorts of data retrieved from Twitter, three journalists from the French paper «Les Échos» were able to illustrate how Twitter has become a powerful tool for Chinese diplomats.
eintraege.gestaltung: I really like it when a Viz is fully integrated in a newspaper full page.

eintraege.kontext: Everybody remembers Gandhi and Nehru, but here is an overview into 50 underrated heroes who were active in the Indian freedom struggle between 1900 to 1947.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular layour with a kind of clevelent chart (inside), labels (middle slice) and bubbles (outside).

eintraege.kontext: Depictions of population movements from and to major German cities, by Zeit Online, the web version of the German newspaper Die Zeit.
eintraege.gestaltung: Beautiful way to show connections on a map. Dark mode is very well done and bundling adds such a nice touch.

eintraege.kontext: Through the use of maps, videos and drawings, Tomas Pueyo gives us a great story about how India just passed China as the most populous country in the world. Spoiler alert: the causes go back a few million years.
eintraege.gestaltung: Very nice storry telling based on various visuals. Note the use of RayShader for the 3d map.

eintraege.kontext: Simran Parwani takes us through her creative dataviz process about the various commercials that are broadcast during the Super Bowl.
eintraege.gestaltung: The streamgraph is very elegant and convey the information efficitently. Note that it is a rare case of vertical streamgraph!

eintraege.kontext: This graphic uses OECD data from 2019-2022 to chart the rise and fall of consumer confidence (expected income and confidence in the economy) in nine major countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: Small multiple is a very powerfull in data visualization. It works even better when all series are repeated but greyed out on all units! 👏

eintraege.titel: The time at which films are born
eintraege.kontext: The 9am Wednesday screenings at the UGC in the Halles district of Paris have become a true barometer to evaluate the success of a film very early on. What are the real correlations? An article by the newspaper Les Échos, and its great scrollytelling version on the web.
eintraege.gestaltung: Very good scrollytelling with animation between chart types. Each dot remains the same thing but moves along the story what allows to keep the focus.

eintraege.kontext: A well-done scrollytelling to understand how the French legislative elections work, using an imaginary « Circular Republic ». By the French newspaper Les Échos.
eintraege.gestaltung: An awesome scrollytelling animating from a voronoi treemap to a circular packing to a barplot.

eintraege.titel: Who speaks about whom in The Office
eintraege.kontext: A visualization showing who the main characters of the tv show The Office mention by name, and how often.
eintraege.gestaltung: Using the small multiples technique with a set of chord diagram is a nice way to show the various flows of this dataset.

eintraege.kontext: The cartography of wine, oil and fruit in southwestern Europe.
eintraege.gestaltung: A bubble map showing both a numeric value (area of culture) and a categoric one (type of culture)

eintraege.kontext: Visualisation of the ambient noise during parisian subway journeys, with algorithmically generated melodies.
eintraege.gestaltung: Pretty hard to describe this chart type as it goes more into data art than data analysis 🙃

eintraege.kontext: Visualisation of the ambient noise during parisian subway journeys, with algorithmically generated melodies.
eintraege.gestaltung: Pretty hard to describe this chart type as it goes more into data art than data analysis 🙃

eintraege.kontext: French legislation aims to prohibit air connections for which there is an alternative by train in less than 2h30. A measure emptied of its initial substance, which will have limited consequences in the fight against global warming.
eintraege.gestaltung: Connection map. Note the usage of arcs and not lines to show the connections.

eintraege.kontext: Using different types of graphs, this article shows how, all over the world, migrants' search interests differ from migration realities.
eintraege.gestaltung: Stunning project with so much information packed into this circular layout.

eintraege.titel: A day in the life of Americans
eintraege.kontext: A animated simulation of 1000 Americans' average day, from sleeping to working, leisure, and all other activities that tend to take place in a 24 hour time span.

Europe has been actively working to reduce CO2 emissions, with many countries implementing diverse strategies based on their economic structures and policies. This has resulted in varying levels of emissions across the region.
eintraege.gestaltung: The Choropleth map features a well-crafted legend that guides viewers through different levels of CO2 emissions. It includes clear annotations and uses a vibrant color scheme, making it both engaging and informative.

eintraege.kontext: COVID-19 has had a major economic impact on most countries in the world, and unemployment is no exception. Most regions have seen dramatic changes in their unemployment rates in a very short space of time, but some have managed to remain stable.
eintraege.gestaltung: This small multi-line graph shows all 9 lines on each of its sub-graphs, but only one of them is highlighted at a time, making it easy to understand how each country's metric system evolved over the period, thanks to a clear colour scheme and precise annotations using arrows.

eintraege.kontext: The Earth's crust is divided into several plates that float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere. When these plates move, they can collide, pull apart, or slide past each other.
eintraege.gestaltung: This bubble map illustrates that points can be used to represent the shape of tectonic plates. The low opacity of the bubbles, the absence of borders between countries and the clear annotations make it easy to read and quickly understand the position of earthquakes around the world.

eintraege.kontext: The number of new films released each year has never been higher, but if we look at the average rating per year, we see that this doesn't mean they're any better, especially when compared to iconic films such as The Godfather.
eintraege.gestaltung: This chart is a combination of a word cloud in the background and a line graph in the foreground. The word cloud is based on film titles to highlight the most common words, while the line graph is very minimalist to display only relevant information.

eintraege.titel: Evolution of number of natural disasters
eintraege.kontext: There are different types of natural disaster, but most tend to increase in frequency every year. In today's world, there is an average of at least one natural disaster every day. Most of these are floods or extreme weather events.
eintraege.gestaltung: This stacked area chart uses arrows with an inflection point in combination with a relevant colour scheme to help the user quickly understand what each element is and measures.

eintraege.kontext: The Fiscal Sponsorship Directory is an organisation that provides a comprehensive list of fiscal sponsorship opportunities, searchable by state and service category. Its aim is to help people find a non-profit organisation for their project when they need help with financial management.
eintraege.gestaltung: This bar chart features a relevant colour scheme that makes it easy to understand which category each bar relates to. What's more, the curved arrows add a pleasant touch.

eintraege.titel: Human Development Index in Sao Paulo
eintraege.kontext: This visualization shows the Human Development Index (HDI) at the subregional level in Sao Paulo, Brazil’s largest city. The values follow the standard United Nations’s HDI: values are in the 0 to 1 range.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a clean choropleth map with a histogram on the side. The histogram is great as it gives additional context to the map and serves as a legend

eintraege.kontext: Climate change, and in particular rising temperatures, is one of the major issues of the 21st century. We are predicting a warming of around 1.5° Celsius by 2050, and 2 to 4° Celsius by 2100.
eintraege.gestaltung: This lollipop plot is beautifully designed with a colour palette from PyPalettes, curved arrows with DrawArrow and cool fonts loaded via PyFonts. It perfectly highlights the rising temperatures we're facing.

eintraege.kontext: For several decades now, Japan's population has been growing more slowly, and has even been declining since 2010. This trend appears to be continuing, even though Japan is losing around 0.5% of its population every year.
eintraege.gestaltung: This minimalist graph changes colour when the values fall below 0, underlining the fact that this is a major change. What's more, the annotations around the graph provide the key contextual information you need.

eintraege.kontext: Climate change is affecting weather patterns across the board. Although extreme heat often takes the spotlight, winter conditions are shifting as well. The 2022–2023 winter season experienced unexpected shifts in both the timing and locations of snowfall.
eintraege.gestaltung: This display is a combination of a hexagonal map and a lollipop-shaped graph. The x-axis of the lollipop is actually the longitude, which makes it easier to read the map and draw parallels.

eintraege.kontext: The chart shows that infant death rates are significantly higher on the first day of life, but decrease sharply in the following days and continue to decline over the year. Over time, the overall curve has shifted down, indicating that infant survival has improved, making every day of infancy safer compared to previous decades.
eintraege.gestaltung: This graph uses one line per year, and even if the trend is not displayed on the x or y axis, the trend over time can be quickly understood thanks to the data and a relevant colour pattern.

eintraege.kontext: This graph shows the evolution of film themes containing the word ‘summer’, according to IMDb data.
eintraege.gestaltung: The sankey diagram highlights the trend at a glance, while the annotations give us more information about the data.

eintraege.kontext: This graph shows the recycling rates for each London borough, highlighting significant differences: some boroughs recycle 17% (minimum) and others nearly 50%.
eintraege.gestaltung: The waffle charts are represented in such a way that the overall figure has the same shape as that of London and each borough is well located.

eintraege.kontext: This graph shows the proportion of cereals used for animal feed on different continents.
eintraege.gestaltung: Using the waffle chart to highlight the differences between the continents makes it much easier to understand and compare them.

eintraege.titel: Gap between Americans' prosperity and well-being
eintraege.kontext: The U.S. has the world's second largest economy. However, many other measures of well-being is far worse than other rich countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: Using the slope chart to highlight the change in ranking between United States and dozen other countries on economic performance, physical health, social trust and more.

eintraege.kontext: One time where celebrities get huge attention is when news break about their death. At least that's what the data shows. Using Wikipedia pageviews, The Pudding examined some notable figures — even those who didn't get much notice until after their passing.
eintraege.gestaltung: Ridgeline chart shows one-week moving average of the percent increase in pageviews compared to the pre-death average. Includes interactive popups to reveal more information among each individual.

eintraege.titel: A Visual History of Which Countries Have Dominated the Summer Olympics
eintraege.kontext: Which countries have acquired more medal during the olympics? The New York Times traced medal counts of participating countries covering from the first game in Athens in 1896 to recent summer olympics held in Rio.
eintraege.gestaltung: Streamgraph in the article shows rise and fall of each country's medal count over time. Besides the time flow of each event, there are streamgraphs concentrated by discipline. Definitely an interesting piece to check out.

eintraege.kontext: A look at high school grades in Alberta using the province's open data. Website targets parents of children about to enter high school, providing comparison of grades among different schools.
eintraege.gestaltung: Website shows average grade by school and subject. Allows interactive to see which school excels in certain subject. For example, can select school that is specifically strong in English education.

eintraege.kontext: Covid-19 pandemic has changed the lives, cautioning people with what to do and how to act accordingly. Schema, parted with Google Trends and Axios, along with art direction from Alberto Cairo, analyzed coronavirus-related search queries to identify what type of information people have been seeking.
eintraege.gestaltung: Using x-axis as the timeline during the pandemic, each bubble represents a query that was among the top trending searches in one or more US states on each day.

eintraege.titel: Americans Say High Prices Are Hitting the Things They Need to Get By
eintraege.kontext: Where have Americans felt inflation at? The New York Times Asked 2,200 people to name specific products and services whose higher prices have stood out to them over the past year.
eintraege.gestaltung: Word cloud lists specific items for which repondents have noticed rising prices. Food items are highlighted orange, others in gray.

eintraege.titel: How Electricity Is Changing, Country by Country
eintraege.kontext: How has electricity generation changed around the world? Using estimated made by Ember, an energy think tank, The New York Times visualizes trends of electricity generation, compared among different countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each area stacked represents energy, categorized under clean power or fossil fuel. The color distinction shows how much fossil-fueled power generation has declined over years.

eintraege.titel: Here Is All the Science at Risk in Trump's Clash With Harvard
eintraege.kontext: The New York Times analyzed terminated grants worth $2.6 billion at Harvard. The article covers which research funding the government has cut and its overall impact.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each treemap, divided under different research categories, shows which research funding had the most impact. At the end of the article is the full interactive treemap, where you can explore more into each canceled grants.

eintraege.kontext: Age distribution across all 550 occupation in the U.S, using data in 2014. The size of the circle shows how many people are employed in that occupation. Bar chart within each circle is the distribution of 7 different age groups.
eintraege.gestaltung: A cool interaction by either entering a specific occupation in a search bar or clicking any of the circles to zoom in.

eintraege.kontext: Not sure how much flour, sugar, or other ingredients you'll need? This visualization breaks down the exact amounts required for different bakes.
eintraege.gestaltung: The sankey diagram highlights how each recipe flows into its ingredients.

eintraege.titel: Breaking the cycle of homelessness in San Francisco — radial dendrogram
eintraege.kontext: A report by Crankstart, a San Francisco'based family foundation, addresses San Francisco's homelessness and offers a road map for administrations to build a better system with demonstrable results.
eintraege.gestaltung: A radial dendrogram arranging 232 service providers around a circle, with curved links connecting them to City agencies (DPH, MOHCD, HSH, etc.) and to three homelessness states. It visualizes the dense, complex ecosystem of support relationships.

eintraege.kontext: Which animal lives the longest? This project uses average life expectancy to calculate and visualize life span of animals.
eintraege.gestaltung: You can either hover over each bubbles to identify which animal or filter using the search bar on the right.

eintraege.kontext: Film directors often favor certain actors, casting them repeatedly across their works. This graph, based on Wes Anderson's ten films and their cast lists, illustrates how frequently specific actors appear in his movies.
eintraege.gestaltung: The upper node in sankey diagram lists 10 films by Wes Anderson. The lower node shows list of actors that appeared repeatedly in his films. If you mouse over each flow, you can find out which actor played which role in a specific movie.

eintraege.kontext: Survey Moneky, in partnership with Axios, collected polls for the 2020 election. They asked each stat whether they were to vote by mail.
