eintraege.gestaltung: Map divides each state into separate hexbins. Darker purple means state is more likely to vote by mail, and vice versa. Good to see annotation of the state name and percentage for each hexbin.

eintraege.titel: The Lifespan of News Stories — area chart
eintraege.kontext: In collaboration between Schema, Google News Initiative, Alberto Cairo, and Axios, the project analyzes search interest data of the top news stories of 2018.
eintraege.gestaltung: A log-scale area chart tracking the search interest of major 2018 news stories over time, with each colored area showing how stories like Stephen Hawking's death and March for our Lives spike and then fade. Annotations label individual peaks and a category legend and story cards sit below.

eintraege.kontext: Fun little diagram showing the similarities between cat and an inkjet printer.

eintraege.titel: How Drug Overdose Deaths Have Plagued One Generation of Black Men for Decades
eintraege.kontext: The New York Times, in partnership with The Baltimore Banner, Big Local News, and nine other newsrooms, analyzed drug overdose deaths over the past decades. Through data, they found one common trend -- that drug overdose has been prevalent especially among Black men.
eintraege.gestaltung: Heatmap shows Covid deaths among Black men, showing a surge in drug deaths due to fentanyl among men born from 1951 to 1970.

eintraege.titel: Inflation in America: Where are prices rising and falling?
eintraege.kontext: NBC News tracks monthly inflation levels for gas, flights, groceries and more. Data is as of April 28, 2025 and all items are percentage change from year earlier.
eintraege.gestaltung: Heatmap shows inflation levels across a variety of consumer metrics. Includes interactive by hovering over each rectangle to see how much prices have changed from a year ago.

eintraege.kontext: Instead of featuring words that is most common, Anti-Tag Cloud shows words that never appear in a text.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is the Anti-Tag Cloud for Alice in Wonderland. Word size indicates how frequent a word is across other texts. You can pick a different book to visualize via search bar.

eintraege.titel: What our analysis of 900 firms shows about their values — beeswarm
eintraege.kontext: How do employees rate their company's work-life balance? The Economist, in partnership with CultureX, a research and AI firm, measures corporate culture across 900 firms in 19 industries. The measurement expressed in the graph is divided into four: work-life balance, toxic culture, leadership, and agility.
eintraege.gestaltung: A set of horizontal beeswarm plots, one per culture dimension (work-life balance, toxic culture, leadership, agility). Each dot is a company, positioned from worse to better and colored on a red-to-blue diverging scale, with select companies directly labeled.

eintraege.kontext: This project analyzes Shakespear's play, looking at main characters and their spokens words in each scene.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each chord diagram represents Shakespear's play and outer bands represent each scene in the play. Length is determined by percent of total words in the play. The bar plot below each chord diagram makes it easier to determine which character had spoken the most.

eintraege.titel: What do you get when your emotions combine?
eintraege.kontext: Feelings can be a mix of different emotions. Using the emotions featured in Inside Out, Six Seconds shows how feelings overlap with different emotions.
eintraege.gestaltung: The Venn Diagram shows two emotions that are combined, resulting in a specific emotion. Wonder what would happen if the characters from Inside Out 2 gets added.

eintraege.kontext:
How are students observing the world? What's the biggest problem that needs to be addressed? The New York Times for Kids, a monthly print-only section for young readers, visualized a survey of children around the country. The original print was issued on Dec. 31, 2023 but you can also find more about it via The New York Times's project, What's Going On in This Graph

.
eintraege.gestaltung: With aims to educate on how to show survey results and about categorical data, the pie chart shows survey results of children for several questions. With some disagreements over pie chart in mind, still think that it is one of the conventional chart type to introduce to students.

eintraege.kontext: The project uses 2022 BRFSS survey to show the distribution of height and weight of American people.
eintraege.gestaltung: The bubble map with x-axis as weight and y axis and height shows BMI of American adults. Each color represents BMI category and size of square gets larger depending on how common it is among adults. Interesting case of combining bubble chart's x,y coordinates with heatmap.

eintraege.kontext: A project for Wired UK, it shows the use of nuclear reactors from 1950 to 2020.
eintraege.gestaltung: Streamgraph shows usage of nuclear energy, where each color represents usage from a specific country. The annotation includes some main events regarding nuclear energy, suggesting the reason of its decrease. On the top left are area charts, showing status of nuclear reactors over time.

eintraege.titel: From here to there: internal migration in Chile
eintraege.kontext: What are the movement patterns of Chileans within the country? Dataista uses the 2024 Population Census to find out.
eintraege.gestaltung:
The interactive page allows you to explore each cicles, which represent each commune. The arcs show how people are moving from one commune to another. You can also read the full article

.

eintraege.titel: A Promising Horizon: How the 2025-2027 Horizon Europe strategic plan will shape Europe's tomorrow — slope chart
eintraege.kontext: One of the three EU's Data Stories created by Nadieh Bremer, the first piece explores the 2025-2027 Horizon Europe strategic plan that plans to invest in circular economy, space, and AI.
eintraege.gestaltung: A slope chart comparing EU member states' raw material consumption per capita between 2013 and 2023, with the EU average drawn in turquoise and Finland, Sweden and Malta highlighted in pink while all other countries are greyed out.

eintraege.titel: Leisure in Europe: Insights from open data — bubble grid
eintraege.kontext: Second piece for EU's Data Stories, created by Nadieh Bremer, covers leisure, culture and tourism in Europe.
eintraege.gestaltung: A small-multiples grid where each EU country is shown as a single circle scaled to the share of household spending on dining out, colored by European region. A legend maps the four region colors and a plate-and-cutlery pictogram anchors the EU average.

eintraege.titel: Health and well-being in the EU: Investing where it matters — Voronoi treemap
eintraege.kontext: The last piece for the European Union, this project uses open data on healthcare spending to analyze healthcare access throughout the EU.
eintraege.gestaltung: A single large circular Voronoi treemap showing the leading causes of death in the EU in 2022, grouped into preventable (44%), treatable (23%) and unavoidable (33%) categories. Each cell is a specific cause of death scaled by the number of deaths, color-coded by category.

eintraege.titel: How far can you go by train from Paris?
eintraege.kontext: An animated visualization that shows train travel times across Europe.
eintraege.gestaltung: The animation makes it hundred times more fascinating, strongly recommend to check out the link below.

eintraege.kontext: A tweet by Donald Trump displaying a choropleth map of the 2016 election results. The map appears to suggest Trump’s victory but is misleading because it ignores the population size of each state.
eintraege.gestaltung: To be more specific, the colors misrepresent the population of each state, giving small and large states equal visual weight. A better alternative would be a bubble map, where each bubble represents a state and is sized according to its population. For a deeper discussion of this misleading map, see this newsletter

eintraege.titel: How TikTok keeps its users scrolling for hours a day
eintraege.kontext: Using 800 Tiktok userss in U.S., The Washington Post analyzes why people become power users, spending hours per day scrolling.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each circle in the chart represents the daily watch time of a real TikTok user, with color scales that show percent change of users from April, 2024.

eintraege.titel: A Data Love Letter to the Subway
eintraege.kontext: A data-driven animation for Fulton Center commissioned by MTA Arts & Design for its 40th annivery. Pentagram, in partnership with Giorgia Lupi, uses MTA data to visualize each train line as a character with its unique personality.
eintraege.gestaltung: The two-minute animation that can be viewed at Fulton Center, New York, is another great example of how everyday data can be turned into beautiful visualization. For example, sankey chart shows each train's final destinations.

eintraege.titel: A Data Love Letter to the Subway
eintraege.kontext: A data-driven animation for Fulton Center commissioned by MTA Arts & Design for its 40th annivery. Pentagram, in partnership with Giorgia Lupi, uses MTA data to visualize each train line as a character with its unique personality.
eintraege.gestaltung: The two-minute animation that can be viewed at Fulton Center, New York, is another great example of how everyday data can be turned into beautiful visualization. For example, barplot shows each train's duration of train spent underground.

eintraege.titel: How mega batteries are unlocking an energy revolution
eintraege.kontext: How does California use solar power at night? The answer lies in grid scale batteries. This visual story from Financial Times highlights the increasing importance of storage solutions for clean energy.
eintraege.gestaltung: The stacked area chart shows California's average energy in a day. Different energy use is represented according to the hour of the day. You can see that solar power is at its peak from early morning to late afternoon.

eintraege.kontext: A project for week 41 of #TidyTuesday, data on food security comes from The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), celebrating World Food Day.
eintraege.gestaltung: The Voronoi treemap shows the average protein supply for different continents. Areas indicate the total protein supply per day for each country.  Nice annotations for specific countries with interesting findings!

eintraege.titel: Where can Americans afford to live solo in 2025?
eintraege.kontext: The Economist, usings its Carrie Bradshaw Index (from Sex and the City, a TV series), ranks 100 of the United States' cities by affordability for living solo.
eintraege.gestaltung: Lollipop chart highlights the gap between median wage and affordable-studio wage for each city. Colors represent affordability(red as unaffordable, blue as affordable). The chart is interactive, so you get choose specific cities, highly recommend to check it out!

eintraege.titel: Here's how Africa wants to redraw the world map
eintraege.kontext: Africa is calling for a change in world map, replacing the widely-used Mercator projection. Reason lies on underestimating the true size of Africa. The Washington Post, visualizes the difference between Mercator and the newly suggested map, Equal Earth.
eintraege.gestaltung: Cartogram shows relative sizes of countries in different map projections. You can spot the stark size-difference between Greenland and Africa, a well-known example of distortion found in Mercator.

eintraege.titel: Tawny frogmouth named 2025 Australian bird of the year winner
eintraege.kontext: Probably one of the most anticipated event for bird lovers, The Guardian Australia has announced the bird of the year for 2025, with more than 310,000 votes casted. The article includes charts from past votes (in 2025 and 2023).
eintraege.gestaltung: The bump chart ranks birds by votes casted for each round (8 round in total). There are filter options for difference highlights including the top ten and big climbs.

eintraege.titel: Bird migration is changing. What does this reveal about our planet? -visualized
eintraege.kontext: The Guardian has tracked bird migration via GPS data. Using animation and map charts, the article explains how climate change has impacted bird travel.
eintraege.gestaltung: The animated map shows seasonal bird migration. Darker green means denser green new life. You can see the seasonal change and migration flow through animation.

eintraege.titel: Bird migration is changing. What does this reveal about our planet? -visualized
eintraege.kontext: The Guardian has tracked bird migration via GPS data. Using animation and map charts, the article explains how climate change has impacted bird travel.
eintraege.gestaltung: Birds tend to move to regions with milder climate. The animated map shows bird migration to different regions, across the continents.

eintraege.titel: Bird migration is changing. What does this reveal about our planet? -visualized
eintraege.kontext: The Guardian has tracked bird migration via GPS data. Using animation and map charts, the article explains how climate change has impacted bird travel.
eintraege.gestaltung: Mario is one of Desertas petrels, bird species known for foraging deep-sea creatures by chasing hurricanes. The map shows Mario's journey, crossing the Atlantic Ocean in different seasons.

eintraege.titel: A Classic Graphic Reveals Nature's Most Efficient Traveler
eintraege.kontext: Science American has updated its graphic, comparing lomotion in the animal kingdom.
eintraege.gestaltung: Chart shows relation between body weight and cost of transport, with each dot representing a specific animal.

eintraege.titel: Women face higher rates of severe food insecurity in most countries
eintraege.kontext: For week 41 of #TidyTuesday, Georgios Karamanis explores global differences in severe food insecurity between women and men.
eintraege.gestaltung: 78 countries are listed horizontally according to its difference of food insecurity betweeen women and men. You can see that countries including Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Peru report higher food insecurity for women.

eintraege.kontext: Using global inflation data, the visualization shows how inflation has spread across different income groups for each country.
eintraege.gestaltung: Barcode charts are divided according to each income levels, with each stripe(country) placed according to the level of inflation.

eintraege.kontext: The Repair Café in Europe is a community-based meeting place where people bring broken items for repairment. The project explores which items has been successfully fixed between 2015 and 2025.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each bubble represents certain group of items, distinguished by color. Each groups of bubbles are along the y-axis, distributed according to the success rate shown in the x-axis.

eintraege.titel: Every Writer of Chris Carter's TV Shows
eintraege.kontext: This project features screenwriters who took part in Chris Carter's TV shows, displaying the summary of contributions for each TV series.
eintraege.gestaltung: Cool infographic with interactive tools such as the sort options by first names, episode counts, and more. Definitely a lot of information to absorb, but the creator has nicely added a 'show legend' button on the bottom to explain how to read the chart.

eintraege.titel: Your diet's impact on the planet depends on where you live. Look up your city.
eintraege.kontext: The 'carbon hoofprint' refers to the amount of climate threat Americans poses from raising meat (beef, pork, and chicken). However, the degree of pollution differs according to each region, according to experts. The Washington Post has visualized its impact across difference regions within the United States.
eintraege.gestaltung: Map shows which regions are concentrated with emissions from meat consumption.

eintraege.titel: China's power over rare earths is not as great as it seems.
eintraege.kontext: An interactive article by The Economist explains in-depth of the recent global tension over rare earth minerals.
eintraege.gestaltung: The stacked area chart shows how much China is leading in production of rare earths.

eintraege.titel: China's power over rare earths is not as great as it seems.
eintraege.kontext: An interactive article by The Economist explains in-depth of the recent global tension over rare earth minerals.
eintraege.gestaltung: Sankey chart shows rare earth flows into specific purposes, leading to more general contributions like manufacturing and electronics.

eintraege.titel: China's power over rare earths is not as great as it seems.
eintraege.kontext: An interactive article by The Economist explains in-depth of the recent global tension over rare earth minerals.
eintraege.gestaltung: Map with different shapes (circles and diamond) show which countries are holding control of rare-earth projects in other regions.

eintraege.titel: What Qualifies as Middle-Income in Each State
eintraege.kontext: Middle income range differs based on where you live. Using data from the five-year American Community Survey from 2023, Nathan Yau explores which region in the U.S has the largest range.
eintraege.gestaltung: You get to interact by choosing the number of household in the filter option.

eintraege.kontext: A visualization for Greenpeace, Nadieh Bremer has created sales of hazardous pesticides by the CropLife companies.
eintraege.gestaltung: The voronoi treemap highlights how five largest agrochemical companies are gaining most profit by selling highly hazardous pesticides. Colors indicate which hazard categories pesticides are part of. For more information of its process, check out her blog

eintraege.titel: Removing content quotas has decimated Australian children's TV
eintraege.kontext: One big chart features hand-drawn charts on key issues from Guardian Australia's data team. This chart shows total hours of children's TV produced in Australia.
eintraege.gestaltung: Love the hand-made chart! You can also check the making of the chart here .

eintraege.kontext: A submission for day 6 of the #30DayMap Challenge , which is a daily mapping challenge taking place every November, Nicola Rennie explores annual rainfall in the UK.
Alvin Chang from The Pudding has done it again with an amazing scrollytelling article. Interactive dot shows every time someone says 'democracy' in the Congressioanl Record since 1880.
eintraege.gestaltung: While ordinary dots represent mentioning of the word, brighter dots are the ones where ones argue American democracy is under threat. The scrollytelling, done in a time series order with dots pouring below text, ultimately leads to a histogram for better exploration. Make sure to check it out!

eintraege.kontext: Earth's land surface account for mere 27%, with the rest all water. This project shows visualization of land, comparing its mass among continents.
eintraege.gestaltung: Voronoi treemap shows proportions of land for each continent.

eintraege.titel: Brussels. A lovely Melting Pot. — voronoi treemap
eintraege.kontext: A data viz essay exploring Brussels and its people.
eintraege.gestaltung: Three side-by-side circular charts on a light background showing where foreigners in Brussels come from, broken down by continents, subregions, and countries. The leftmost pies progress into a voronoi-style treemap of countries on the right, each accompanied by a ranked legend with percentages and counts.

eintraege.titel: The Chart Contains a Few Hidden Surprises About the Economy
eintraege.kontext: An article with neat visual to show proportions of global GDP each countries takes up.
eintraege.gestaltung: Voronoi treemap shows countries with size relative to the amount of global GDP is takes up. We can spot the two biggest economic countributers (U.S. and China) right on.

eintraege.titel: Mapping the future of the AU-EU partnership — infrastructure map
eintraege.autor: European Union Institute for Security Studies (EUISS)
eintraege.kontext: In partnership between the European Union (EU) and the African Union (AU), The European Union Institute for Security Studies published a data-heavy report on EU-AU relations.
eintraege.gestaltung: A detailed reference map of Africa plotting transport and settlement infrastructure: airports, ports, roads, railroads, urban areas and water bodies, with a categorical legend on a light background.

eintraege.kontext: Which countries' citizens get to travel to which countries, visa-free? Ihar Yanouski uses passport index data to visualize which destinations with a certain visa regime for every country.
eintraege.gestaltung: The interactive visualization allows you to click on either country in map or via search bar to see the flow of map according to visa restriction. Definitely a fun yet informative project to interact with!

eintraege.kontext: Using charts and illustrations, the article explains about spina bifida, one of the most common serious birth conditions that is yet unknown to many.
eintraege.gestaltung: One of the chart in the article is proportional area chart, which compares two datasets (in this case, continent/incontinent). Size refers to proportion to each measurement.

eintraege.kontext: Does U.S. chocolate taste poorly compared to the same ones produced in Europe? Surbhi Bhatia uses data of each chocolate ingredients to find it out.
eintraege.gestaltung: Two triangular radar charts comparing US versus UK versions of Dairy Milk and Kit Kat across sugar, fat, and cocoa, with annotated callouts highlighting that the US versions have more sugar, less fat, and less chocolate.

eintraege.kontext: For 2025's #30DayMapChallenge Day 25: Hexagons, Ansgar Wolsing uses population data to visualize share of population aged 15-24 in Germany.
eintraege.gestaltung: Strong visual that displays concentration of youth in certain regions.

eintraege.titel: Should you take the train or the car?
eintraege.kontext: For 2025's #30dDayMapChallenge transports, Jules Grandin explores map of the fastest mode of transport from 10 major French cities.
eintraege.gestaltung: The difference between traveling through train (blue) and car (purple) builds up as each color darkens, love it!

eintraege.titel: Comparison of the environmental impacts of agricultural production
eintraege.kontext: Benjamin Nowak uses data of environmental footprint required to produce 1kg of milk, meat, grain or fruit.
eintraege.gestaltung: Instead of the conventional radar chart that we expect of, a symbolic 'flower' is used to represent environmental footprint. The size of each petal corresponds to type of impact, with largest petal represention the production with greatest impact.

eintraege.titel: Young adult's personalities are changing, with conscientiousness in freefall
eintraege.kontext: The Financial Times uses data with different age groups to visualize the downfall of consciousness that is especially strong among young adults.
eintraege.gestaltung: One simple line chart suggesting interesting trend of consciousness in freefall.

eintraege.kontext: One of Diana MacDonald's complete 30 day chart challenge for 2025, this visualization lists ACT Threatened Species including a cute Scarlet Robin.
eintraege.gestaltung: If you are curious to explore more, make sure to check out the complete collection through the link below!

eintraege.titel: Are you in TikTok's cat niche? What 121,000 videos reveal.
eintraege.kontext: Did you know cat videas are often watched by people who also enjoy LGBTQ+ and music content? That's what The Washington Post says according to an analysis based on watch histories provided by 1,100 tiktok users.
eintraege.gestaltung: Along various topics that are clustered according to TikTok's algorithm, the hexbin map shows which hastag is opposite to which hastags.

eintraege.titel: The Physical Phenomenon: Why CDs are still well-loved in Kpop
eintraege.kontext: Popularity of kpop and its kpop merch frenzy comes with a cost. The Kontinentalist visualizes how album sales from Kpop has exponentially increased, with physical albums posing as an environmental concern.
eintraege.gestaltung: Size of icon means amount of albums sold. For more information, you can mouse over each icons.

eintraege.titel: Business is booming for defense contractors
eintraege.kontext: Military spending has risen over the past years worldwide. Which would mean new recording revenues for defense industries. Reuters visualizes  top defense companies for dominant countries and regions.
eintraege.gestaltung: Using circular packing, each big circle represents either a country or a region. The nested circles represent defense companies and its size correspond to revenue from arms sales.

eintraege.titel: How Much Snow Will Fall Where You Live?
eintraege.kontext: Will we be celebrating White Christmas for 2025? We could only look to weather forecasts to give our best guess. The New York Times uses weather forecaster to visualize the likeliness to snow in the United States.
eintraege.gestaltung: The data is updated with the newly issued data noted below the map.

eintraege.titel: Who earns a higher salary than you and the jobs they work
eintraege.kontext: Another fun, interactive dataviz by Nathan Yau, the visual allows you to see who makes more than you and in which occupation.
eintraege.gestaltung: You can use the slider to adjust annual salary!

eintraege.kontext: Just how much investment is being made in AI? Reuters says it has already outstripped government-led initiatives like the Manhaten Project and the Apollo program. The article dives into the vast investment that is currently being made.
eintraege.gestaltung: A cool interactive bar chart that compares the invesment that has been made to space projects and AI. If you keep scrolling it shows how AI investment has far passed the other past projects.

eintraege.titel: We asked more than 40 people to track their coffee consumption for a week. Here is what we found.
eintraege.kontext: A delight work by Straits Times, visualizing 40 people of their coffee consumption for a week.
eintraege.gestaltung: Love the part where you customize your own cup of cofee depending on its coffee bean, taste, and the feeling after drinking it.

eintraege.kontext: The visualization uses rents by municipality using data from 9 million rental listings from open data set from the French Ministry of Ecology, Territorial Development, Transport, Urban Affairs and Housing.

eintraege.titel: The Chinese goods Americans most rely on, from microwaves to Barbies
eintraege.kontext: Despite the tariff war between US and China, the reliance on Chinese goods is undeniable. In this piece, Financial Times analyzes which categorized goods the US has been relying most.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each circle represents Chinese goods in a certain categorized, which is distinguished through color. You can easily see which imports are most critical to the tariff Trump adminsistration has imposed.

eintraege.kontext: Georgios Karamanis's submission for #TidyTuesday 2024, week of 44, she uses monster movie titles to look at some of the most frequent words.
eintraege.gestaltung: Love the pumpkin!

eintraege.titel: How Much the Most Followed Instagram Accounts Earn on Posts
eintraege.kontext: We know that a single post from a renowned celebrity can capture the attention of millions. But how powerful is that influence when it comes to money? Visual Capitalist visualizes Instagram's biggest accounts, and their estimated earnings per sponsored post.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each circle represents one celebrity with size corresponding to earnings per post. This kind of new ranking makes it easier for readers to absorb information.

eintraege.kontext: In this article, The Washington Post covers the increasing attempts of Haitians to cross the Bahamian waters for migration. The map visualizes their journey, which often ends up into unfortunate events.
A really cool work of visualization showing ten volcanoes and the record of its eruptions.
eintraege.gestaltung: Love the visualization packed with so many interesting facts!

eintraege.kontext: A circular barplot that shows days of snow and hail in each Italian chief town arranged by season and weather on Christmas day. The data is from 1973~2019.
eintraege.gestaltung: The bars for each plot are arranged in time order clockwise, with height corresponding to weather categories (snow, hail, etc). What an inspiration!

eintraege.kontext: The visualization shows the seized assets (real estates and companies) from organized crime in Italy.
eintraege.gestaltung: If you follow the stream (left to right) you can see new destination of seized assets and new purposes.

eintraege.kontext: What are the top 10 most visited amusement parks in North America? This map visualization uses data of number of visitors in 2016 to find out.
eintraege.gestaltung: Orange bubble represents top 10 most visited amusement parks while light blue bubble represents top 10 water parks in North America.

eintraege.titel: The most friendless place on earth
eintraege.kontext: Does being rich make you lonelier? Well that is not the case when comparing countries by income. The Economist, using data from 2025 or latest available, finds out the the percentage of loneliness people felt.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each line represent countries divided into income level. We can easily see that the ones experiencing more loneliness are the ones in red (low-income countries)

eintraege.titel: What street talk reveals about Alglophone civilisation
eintraege.kontext: For Christmas Specials in 2025, The Economist has used a selection of drinking slang 1500-2020 and put them into a wonderful time-lined word visualization.
eintraege.gestaltung: Love the animation with words poppling up as I scroll down.

eintraege.titel: Why Do Some Americans Leave Their Religion While Others Stay?
eintraege.kontext: An interesting finding from Pew Research Center that 56% of U.S. adults identify with their childhood religion. The original paper goes more in depth to find out the reason behind this.
A map visualization that shows where in the world solstice is/was a ritual celebration.

eintraege.titel: AI Data Center Gold Rush Driven by Thousands of Newcomers
eintraege.kontext: Four major tech companies has been dominating the AI infrastructure game, but there are new players incoming. Bloomberg analyzed thousands of data center operators, visualizing both the current AI data center occupation as well as its future with new players.
eintraege.gestaltung: The scroytelling of current AI data centers in map shows what the future will be like if other firms come to join the race.

eintraege.titel: Who we choose to spend our days with
eintraege.kontext: Who are we spending our days with? Nathan Yau uses American Time User Survey between 2022 and 2024 to show  the distribution of time spent with others.
eintraege.gestaltung: Fun interactive with options to change respondents by sex, age, and time of week.

eintraege.kontext: A powerful visual storytelling about how ICE has moved thousands of people through detention and out of the country.
eintraege.gestaltung: Besides the animated connected map which shows transfers and removals of people, there are additional maps that visualizes where ICE makes arrests and where they are held, all very powerful. Make sure to check them out.

eintraege.titel: Why playful adults help Lego build an empire at Christmas and beyond
eintraege.kontext: Lego, once deemed as a toy for kids, is capturing attention of adults as well. USA Today uses visualizations to explain its growing market.
eintraege.gestaltung: The simple bar chart made with Lego block shows the increasing number of Lego branded stores, worldwide.

eintraege.titel: What if you'd been born somewhere else?
eintraege.kontext: An interesting game where you spin the globe to choose where to be born again, and see your expected life expectancy and child mortality at this new birthplace.

eintraege.titel: More Texas students complete journey through college, but low-income students still left behind
eintraege.kontext: The Texas Tribune uses state data to track how economically disadvantaged students are much less likely to go on and attain degrees.
eintraege.gestaltung: The animated sankey flow shows how economic disadvantage impacts student outcomes. For a more straight-forward result, there is another option to look at waffle chart of the same result.

eintraege.titel: Map: The 2024 European election results in France, town by town
eintraege.kontext: Le Monde visualizes the 2024 European election results in France, town by town.
eintraege.gestaltung: Love the colorblind option below the map chart!

eintraege.titel: Where do all the world's people live?
eintraege.kontext: Information is Beautiful uses United Nation's mid-year predictions for 2023 to visualize country by population.
eintraege.gestaltung: Voronoi treemap shows regions that has been subdivded into each country, with size deteremined by population.

eintraege.kontext: The New York Times has visualized the destruction in Ukraine, using interactive storytelling and data to highlight the damages.
eintraege.gestaltung: Definitely recommend checking out the story, and if you are interested in the visualization process, check out the extensive blog writtern by its creator.

eintraege.kontext: Karim Douïeb uses data from Ipsos to visualize sociology of French electorates.
eintraege.gestaltung: This chart would be Marimekko chart, which has both axes as percentage scales, that deteremines wideth and height of each variables in a certain categorical data.

eintraege.titel: Monitoring forest fires in Europe through high-value datasets
eintraege.kontext: A data viz created by Federica Fragapane using European Union's data on forest fires. You can see the article published by EU here .
eintraege.gestaltung: Voronoi treemap shows goods imported by member state, with each portion of circle representing EU member state.

eintraege.titel: 40,000 tweets in two years: Elon Musk's switch to X dissected
eintraege.kontext: Les Echos has invested 40,000 tweets Elon Musk made in the last two years. Using those data, the visualization shows which topics Elon Musk has focused on his tweet.
A client work from a group that wanted to present a colleague's impact in the company, Tanja Radovanovic uses the collected data to create a time-lined data art.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each plant is one project with biggest flower the main fruit of her work. Love the nice data art guides provided below the work.

eintraege.kontext: A client work for Mozilla, the interactive visualization shows entire commit history of a GitHub repository.
eintraege.gestaltung: Commits grouped by month, each scaled by the number of lines changed, in an interactive timeline where you can explore a commit and jump to others by the same author. More on her blog.

eintraege.titel: More days with less Arctic sea ice
eintraege.kontext: New study shows that first ice-free day in the Arctic Ocean may come beofre 2030. Financial Times uses ridgeline plot to show the change in Arctic sea ice over the years.
eintraege.gestaltung: The distribution moving gradually towards the left shows the decrease in sea ice and what is to come ahead in the future.

eintraege.kontext: The European Correspondent visualizes a survey result that suggests Europeans prefer Kamala Harris to be elected as U.S president over Donald Trump.
eintraege.gestaltung: Nice, clean graph with annotations.

eintraege.titel: Explore the striking political divides across Europe
eintraege.kontext: An interactive map for European elections, where users get to explore voting results across the 27 European Union member states.

eintraege.titel: This is how the AfD brought hatred into parliaments
eintraege.kontext: An extensive scrollytelling analysis of AfD speeches in German state parliament. Throught the speech over the years, there is map highlighting certain regions that has mentioned certain topics more than any other region.
eintraege.gestaltung: Love how they added a barplot below map to show actual mentions over time.

eintraege.titel: Too Much Of A Good Thing
eintraege.kontext: An analysis by The Economist shows that weight is still a critical factor in car crashes in America. Using data, the visualization shows relationship between vehicle weight and road safety.
eintraege.gestaltung: The grey dot represents fatality rate of the occupants of heavy pickup truck while red one represents fatality rate of people in other cars. The following result is that as weight of your car increases, the risk of killing others will increase dramatically.

eintraege.kontext: A voronoi treemap representing TV Series in the Star Trek universe, made with Tableau.
eintraege.gestaltung: Each block represents one season, with size according to number of episodes. Color of block is divided by series.

eintraege.kontext: A submission for #ironviz, data-viz competition using Tableau, Mateusz Karmalski uses James Bond movie data to visualize the film.
eintraege.gestaltung: Love how there is a treemap in the shape of a wine glass!

eintraege.kontext: A visual oveview of rainfall variations across France, highlighting the rainiest regions.

eintraege.titel: Education attainment vs. GDP per Capita PPPs (2005-2023)
eintraege.kontext: This visualization shows education attainment by GDP per Capita PPPs for each country. Using connected scatterplot, it shows sequential nature of the data.
eintraege.gestaltung: The color indicates western (blue) and former communist (red) countries, with height x-axis and y-axis depending on more education and more purschasing power accordingly.

eintraege.kontext: To look at how people in Europe has been feeling lately, The European Correspondent uses survey data to show distribution of different feelings people felt in the previous day.
eintraege.gestaltung: Different categories of feeling each have their own beeswarm according to response. Colors are divided into positive (green) and negative (red).

eintraege.titel: 2025 was the third hottest year in record
eintraege.kontext: When it comes to climate change, you cannot leave out data. The Economist visualizes the global surface air-temperature for the past years.
eintraege.gestaltung: Heatmap shows how temperature has been rising in recent years.

eintraege.kontext: Strong visual showing how much funding has been provided for ICE for the past years.
eintraege.gestaltung: The distinctive orange barplots along with bold annotations highlight the dramatic increase of funding for ICE.

eintraege.titel: What science can tell us about dog breeds
eintraege.kontext: A visualization by Scientific American using data on dog behavior obtained from more than 50,000 owners to categories behaviors by breeds.
eintraege.gestaltung: This is a dot plot with each dot representing a certain dog breed. Color distinctions are made according to typical size. Make sure to check out the article to explore more on other categoreis as well!

eintraege.kontext: An interactive Economist piece on how diverse England has become, and where. With official figures unavailable, they estimated each area's ethnic make-up from the annual census of schoolchildren. More in The Economist: Off the Charts.
eintraege.gestaltung: The scatterplot shows constituencies in England, with areas split into four sections according to diversity and segregation. A search bar allows you to find specific constituency and see which section it belongs to.

eintraege.kontext: A visualization that ranks bird types using data of joy rating for common UK birds.
eintraege.gestaltung: A joy rating for each bird type, with line representing 95% confidence interval.

eintraege.kontext: With the ongoing tensions in Minnesota with federal presence, The Minnesota Star Tribune has visualized what it would look like if additional federal agents were to head to the city.
eintraege.gestaltung: Instead of plain, solid pie chart showing propotions, the pie chart comes in a scatter of numerous dots with each representing one officer. This allows strong visual of how one side outnumbers the other.

eintraege.kontext: A sweet interactive article showing how ranked-choice voting process works for ice-cream.
eintraege.gestaltung: A fun interactive where you first rank five favorite ice cream flavors and follow along the votes getting counted until the final winner is decided.

eintraege.kontext: Americans spend far more on health than any other country, yet live shorter lives than people in other rich countries that spend much less. In the 1970s the US was not an outlier, but since then its health spending has exploded while life expectancy gains stalled — and have recently started to decline.
eintraege.gestaltung: A connected scatterplot where each line is a country, connecting yearly observations from 1970 to 2018: health spending per capita on the x-axis, life expectancy on the y-axis. Greying out every country except the USA (in red) instantly tells the story — the American line drifts far to the right without climbing much, breaking away from the tight cluster of other nations. A textbook example of how highlighting a single series turns a spaghetti of trajectories into a clear message.

eintraege.kontext: A scrollytelling piece by Taiwan's CommonWealth Magazine (天下雜誌) on how Apple's manufacturing supply chain has shifted over the years. In this 2012 snapshot, more than 40% of Apple's suppliers — 333 manufacturing sites — were located in China, by far the largest share in the world.
eintraege.gestaltung: A circular packing chart where each dot is one Apple manufacturing site, nested into bubbles by region. Highlighting China in red against the greyed-out rest makes its dominance obvious. I love the dotted texture inside each circle — it turns an abstract proportion into something you can almost count.

eintraege.kontext: Across five presidential elections from 2004 to 2020, how did each US state's partisan lean shift? This New York Times graphic places every state on a Democratic-to-Republican margin axis for each election year, tracing how solidly blue and red states moved — and which ones flirted with crossing the line.
eintraege.gestaltung: A bump-style line chart: each line is a state, threaded top-to-bottom through the five election years and positioned left-to-right by its voting margin, with a central 'Tie' line as the anchor. Blue and red encode the lean. The result reads almost like flowing currents, and the swings of swing states pop out immediately against the calm of the safe ones.

eintraege.titel: South Gaza's services and a doubling of population
eintraege.kontext: After Israel ordered the evacuation of northern Gaza in October 2023, more than a million people were expected to move south — into an area whose health services are far sparser. Bloomberg maps where people live against how easily they can reach a hospital, before and after the evacuation.
eintraege.gestaltung: A bivariate map blending two variables into one 2D colour scale (see the legend): population density against access to health services. A 'Before / After evacuation' toggle and arrow annotations walk you through the shift. A masterclass in encoding two dimensions on one map without losing the reader.

eintraege.kontext: The covid crisis is a world wide pandemic and India is certainly not spared. Some volunteer decided to create a dashboard to help Indian politics to take information driven decisions.
eintraege.gestaltung: The light-theme breakdown view: a sortable state-by-state table where horizontal bars encode the confirmed, active, recovered and deceased counts for each region, alongside a 'Spread' bar chart of the daily figures. Easy to rank states at a glance.

eintraege.kontext: The covid crisis is a world wide pandemic and India is certainly not spared. Some volunteer decided to create a dashboard to help Indian politics to take information driven decisions.
eintraege.gestaltung: Four headline metrics - confirmed, active, recovered and deceased - each paired with a colour-coded sparkline of its recent trend and the day's increment. The 'Active' card is highlighted in blue. A clean, scannable summary strip.

eintraege.kontext: Covid is everywhere in the news and every newspaper is trying to summarize the situation in its country. Le Monde is one of the most famous newspapers in France and does a pretty good job in its daily updated dashboard.
eintraege.gestaltung: Two side-by-side step line charts comparing hospitalisation and critical-care admission rates per million for vaccinated, boosted, and unvaccinated people. End-of-line labels identify each series and highlighted phrases in the intro text emphasize the key multipliers.

eintraege.kontext: Covid is everywhere in the news and every newspaper is trying to summarize the situation in its country. Le Monde is one of the most famous newspapers in France and does a pretty good job in its daily updated dashboard.
eintraege.gestaltung: A colorful streamgraph showing the distribution of daily Covid deaths across major world regions over time, using a 21-day rolling average. Inline labels sit directly on each flowing band, and a vivid color palette separates Brazil, the US, Europe, India, and Asia.

eintraege.titel: Covid dashboard — area with line overlay
eintraege.kontext: Covid is everywhere in the news and every newspaper is trying to summarize the situation in its country. Le Monde is one of the most famous newspapers in France and does a pretty good job in its daily updated dashboard.
eintraege.gestaltung: A time series of daily critical-care admissions in France, with pale orange bars/area for raw daily values overlaid by a bold smoothed line trend. An annotated open circle and headline call out the latest value of 291 admissions.

eintraege.titel: Rappers, Sorted by Size of Vocabulary — histogram
eintraege.kontext: A projects that compares the number of unique words used by some of the most famous artists in hip hop using each artist’s first 35,000 lyrics. Jedi Mind Tricks used 6424 unique words, compared to DMX that counts 2936.
eintraege.gestaltung: Overlapping histograms comparing the distribution of unique-word counts across three music genres (Country, Rock, Hip Hop) using semi-transparent colored bars. Hip Hop spreads furthest to the right, showing larger vocabularies.

eintraege.titel: Hong Kong and the Omicron variant — line chart
eintraege.kontext: Hong Kong’s vaccination rate has lagged far behind peer countries, especially among the most vulnerable. This article by the financial times goes deep into this matter and compares the situation with other countries.
eintraege.gestaltung: A multi-line time series of cumulative confirmed Covid-19 deaths per million people. Hong Kong's red line surges sharply at the end to overtake its Asia-Pacific peers and several European countries, with each line directly labeled at the right edge.

eintraege.titel: Art, Women posing and upvotes — ridgeline density
eintraege.kontext: Do women who pose with their art on Reddit get more upvotes? Erin gathered reddit data on the topic to proove that yes, posing with your art helps getting upvoted, especially if you're a woman.
eintraege.gestaltung: A small-multiples set of mirrored density distributions (a ridgeline-style back-to-back layout) showing upvote-ratio distributions for women (purple, up) versus men (green, down) across five post-score brackets. Median ratios are directly labeled on each distribution and side annotations narrate the trend.

eintraege.kontext: French presidential elections are happening soon. Le Monde wrote a in-depth article showing some of the candidate features: who talks the most on media, who's the richest, who has the best chances to win according to polls?
eintraege.gestaltung: Scatter plot positioning each candidate by wealth (patrimoine) on the x-axis and income (revenus) on the y-axis, with reference lines marking the French median. Candidates are color-coded with a legend, and notable points are directly annotated.

eintraege.kontext: French presidential elections are happening soon. Le Monde wrote a in-depth article showing some of the candidate features: who talks the most on media, who's the richest, who has the best chances to win according to polls?
eintraege.gestaltung: Bubble map of France showing the number of mayoral endorsements (parrainages) a candidate received per department, with circle size encoding the count. A tooltip reveals details on hover for a selected department, and a thumbnail strip lets users switch between candidates.

eintraege.kontext: The central piece of a study on the spread of QAnon in the german-speaking world. It shows the amount of QAnon related messages exchanged on Telegram.
eintraege.gestaltung: A grouped bar chart comparing the number of QAnon-related posts in channels (orange) versus groups (grey) from 2018 to 2021, showing a dramatic year-over-year increase up to 8.3 million. Exact values are written directly above and below each bar.

eintraege.titel: The Spread of QAnon — small multiples
eintraege.kontext: The central piece of a study on the spread of QAnon in the german-speaking world. It shows the amount of QAnon related messages exchanged on Telegram.
eintraege.gestaltung: Three area charts shown as small multiples, each tracking membership over time for one of the largest QAnon groups. The first panel (Donald J. Trump = Q Family) towers above the others, peaking near 60,000 members in early 2021.

eintraege.titel: Airports and world's megacities — mirror barplot
eintraege.kontext: Biggest cities tend to have more departing flights per day. But some cities don't follow the trend. This data-based article tries to explain it.
eintraege.gestaltung: A back-to-back (mirror) bar chart with population bars extending left and flights-per-day bars extending right for each city, sorted by population. An annotation highlights African megacities like Lagos and Kinshasa that lag in flights.

eintraege.titel: Airports and world's megacities — connected scatter
eintraege.kontext: Biggest cities tend to have more departing flights per day. But some cities don't follow the trend. This data-based article tries to explain it.
eintraege.gestaltung: A connected scatterplot of population versus flights per day, with colored arrows tracing each selected city's trajectory from 2003 to 2018. A dashed reference line marks the 10-million-people threshold.

eintraege.kontext: Biggest cities tend to have more departing flights per day. But some cities don't follow the trend. This data-based article tries to explain it.
eintraege.gestaltung: A scatterplot of population versus flights per day where each dot is a city, colored to distinguish current megacities, probable 2030 megacities, and other 10-million-plus cities. Many points are directly labeled with city names.

eintraege.kontext: An exploration of the dining habits and companions of Americans.
eintraege.gestaltung: An arrow chart split into two age-group panels, where each row uses a directional arrow from 2003 to 2015 to show how the share of meals spent with each companion type shifted, with diamonds marking changes under 0.5%.

eintraege.titel: What is Congress tweeting about? — area chart
eintraege.kontext: An article describing the topics that dominate members of Congress public discourse.
eintraege.gestaltung: A filled area/line chart on a dark background tracking the volume of tweets over a full year, with a subtle gradient fill under a green line and a date axis along the bottom.

eintraege.titel: What is Congress tweeting about? — tile grid map
eintraege.kontext: An article describing the topics that dominate members of Congress public discourse.
eintraege.gestaltung: A tile grid map of the US states, each state shown as an equal-sized square labeled with its abbreviation and shaded in a gold color scale to encode a value. The geographic-style layout flattens states into a uniform grid.

eintraege.titel: Switching between phone brands — full chord diagram
eintraege.kontext: A study asked 2000 residents of the Netherlands about their mobile phone behavior. The respondents gave information about the brand of their current main phone, and the brand of their previous main phone, and their answers are visualized in this data story.
eintraege.gestaltung: The complete chord diagram showing flows of respondents switching between mobile phone brands, with every ribbon drawn at once. Each brand occupies a colored arc around the circle and the ribbon thickness encodes the volume of switching between brand pairs.

eintraege.kontext: Some figures for a shareholder letter & annual report. Four extensive visuals about the income statement, costs, regional and FTE growth.
eintraege.gestaltung: A treemap breaking down total costs, with rectangles rotated 45 degrees and a hatched texture on selected cells. A secondary detail treemap expands the 'Other operating expenses' category, with labels set directly along the tilted edges.

eintraege.kontext: Some figures for a shareholder letter & annual report. Four extensive visuals about the income statement, costs, regional and FTE growth.
eintraege.gestaltung: Small-multiple waffle charts comparing the number of employees per city between 2017 and 2018, with each office shown as a 45-degree rotated diamond unit. Cities are sorted by size with before/after counts labelled directly under each grid.

eintraege.kontext: Each year, US cities give thousands of homeless people one-way bus tickets out of town. An 18-month nationwide investigation by the Guardian reveals, for the first time, what really happens at journey’s end.

eintraege.gestaltung: A heatmap showing how African countries voted against the African majority at the UN over time, with countries on the y-axis and years on the x-axis, encoded by colored cells alongside an explanatory text block.

eintraege.autor: European Union Institute for Security Studies (EUISS)
eintraege.kontext: In partnership between the European Union (EU) and the African Union (AU), The European Union Institute for Security Studies published a data-heavy report on EU-AU relations.
eintraege.gestaltung: A grid of small-multiple line charts on education indicators, one minimalist sparkline-style trend per country, arranged in a tidy matrix with direct country labels.

eintraege.autor: European Union Institute for Security Studies (EUISS)
